# Page: Tensor Parallelism Support

# Tensor Parallelism Support

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [flash_attn/models/gpt.py](flash_attn/models/gpt.py)
- [flash_attn/modules/block.py](flash_attn/modules/block.py)
- [flash_attn/modules/mha.py](flash_attn/modules/mha.py)
- [flash_attn/modules/mlp.py](flash_attn/modules/mlp.py)
- [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py](flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py)
- [tests/modules/test_mlp_parallel.py](tests/modules/test_mlp_parallel.py)

</details>



This page documents the tensor parallelism (TP) support in FlashAttention, which enables training and inference of large models by partitioning weights across multiple GPUs. Tensor parallelism splits individual weight matrices along specific dimensions, allowing models that exceed single-GPU memory capacity to run efficiently across multiple devices.

For information about model integration and loading pretrained weights, see [GPT-Style Model Architecture](#11.2). For details about the attention mechanisms themselves, see [MHA and ParallelMHA Modules](#11.1).

## Overview

Tensor parallelism in FlashAttention follows Megatron-LM's column/row parallelism pattern, where:
- **Column Parallelism**: Weight matrix is split along the output dimension, requiring an all-gather before the operation and no communication after
- **Row Parallelism**: Weight matrix is split along the input dimension, requiring no communication before but a reduce-scatter after
- **Sequence Parallelism**: Additionally splits the batch×sequence dimension across ranks to reduce memory usage for activations and enable all-reduce fusion with gradient computation

The implementation supports both standalone tensor parallelism and sequence parallelism modes, configurable per-layer through the `sequence_parallel` flag.

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:1-247]()

## Architecture Overview

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Tensor Parallel Data Flow"
        Input["Input Tensor<br/>(batch, seqlen, hidden_dim)"]
        
        subgraph "Sequence Parallel Mode"
            SPScatter["scatter_to_sequence_parallel_region<br/>Split on seqlen dimension"]
            LocalInput["Local Input<br/>(batch, seqlen/world_size, hidden_dim)"]
            SPScatter --> LocalInput
        end
        
        subgraph "Column Parallel Layer"
            AllGather1["all_gather_raw<br/>Gather across ranks"]
            FullInput["Full Input<br/>(batch, seqlen, hidden_dim)"]
            ColWeight["Weight (split)<br/>(out_features/world_size, in_features)"]
            ColMatmul["F.linear<br/>output_local"]
            
            AllGather1 --> FullInput
            FullInput --> ColMatmul
            ColWeight --> ColMatmul
        end
        
        subgraph "Row Parallel Layer"
            RowWeight["Weight (split)<br/>(out_features, in_features/world_size)"]
            RowMatmul["F.linear<br/>output_local"]
            ReduceScatter["reduce_scatter_raw<br/>Sum+Split across ranks"]
            LocalOutput["Local Output<br/>(batch, seqlen/world_size, out_features)"]
            
            RowWeight --> RowMatmul
            RowMatmul --> ReduceScatter
            ReduceScatter --> LocalOutput
        end
        
        Input --> SPScatter
        Input -.No SP.-> AllGather1
        LocalInput --> AllGather1
        ColMatmul --> RowMatmul
    end
    
    subgraph "Backward Pass"
        GradOut["Grad Output"]
        GradWeight["Grad Weight<br/>(computed locally)"]
        GradInput["Grad Input<br/>(reduce_scatter or all_reduce)"]
        
        GradOut --> GradWeight
        GradOut --> GradInput
    end
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:27-116](), [flash_attn/utils/distributed.py]()

## Parallel Linear Layers

### ColumnParallelLinear

`ColumnParallelLinear` splits the weight matrix along the output dimension (columns). Each rank holds a slice of shape `(out_features/world_size, in_features)`.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Forward Pass"
        X["x<br/>(batch, in_features)"]
        AG["all_gather<br/>(if sequence_parallel)"]
        FullX["total_x<br/>(batch, in_features)"]
        W["Weight Slice<br/>(local_out, in_features)"]
        Out["output<br/>(batch, local_out)"]
        
        X --> AG
        AG --> FullX
        FullX --> Matmul
        W --> Matmul
        Matmul["F.linear"] --> Out
    end
    
    subgraph "Backward Pass"
        dOut["grad_output"]
        dW["grad_weight<br/>(computed on total_x)"]
        dX["grad_input<br/>(matmul with W.t())"]
        RS["reduce_scatter<br/>(if sequence_parallel)"]
        
        dOut --> dW
        dOut --> dX
        dX --> RS
    end
```

Key implementation details:
- **Uneven splits**: Uses `get_dim_for_local_rank()` to handle `out_features` not evenly divisible by `world_size`
- **Sequence parallel**: When enabled, performs `all_gather_raw()` before the matmul to reconstruct the full input tensor
- **Bias handling**: Bias is replicated across all ranks (each rank has the same bias slice)

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:166-203]()

### RowParallelLinear

`RowParallelLinear` splits the weight matrix along the input dimension (rows). Each rank holds a slice of shape `(out_features, in_features/world_size)`.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Forward Pass"
        X["x<br/>(batch, local_in)"]
        W["Weight Slice<br/>(out_features, local_in)"]
        LocalOut["local_output<br/>(batch, out_features)"]
        RS["reduce_scatter or all_reduce"]
        FinalOut["output<br/>(batch, out_features)"]
        
        X --> Matmul
        W --> Matmul
        Matmul["F.linear"] --> LocalOut
        LocalOut --> RS
        RS --> FinalOut
    end
    
    subgraph "Bias Handling"
        Rank0["Rank 0: has bias"]
        OtherRanks["Rank 1-N: bias=None"]
    end
```

Key implementation details:
- **No all-gather needed**: Input is already partitioned appropriately
- **Reduce operation**: Uses `reduce_scatter` (sequence parallel) or `all_reduce` (non-sequence parallel) to combine results
- **Bias on rank 0 only**: Only rank 0 holds the bias vector; other ranks have `bias=None` to avoid duplicate addition during all-reduce

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:206-246]()

### FusedDenseFunc

`FusedDenseFunc` is the underlying autograd function that implements optimized forward/backward passes with tensor parallelism:

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| Forward dtype casting | Automatic conversion to `torch.get_autocast_gpu_dtype()` when autocast enabled |
| Async communication | Uses `async_op=True` for overlapping all-gather with weight conversion |
| Backward gradient accumulation | Uses `fused_dense_cuda.linear_bias_wgrad()` for fused weight+bias gradients |
| Return residual | Optional residual return for post-norm architectures with fused backward |

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:27-115]()

## Sequence Parallelism

Sequence parallelism extends tensor parallelism by also partitioning activations along the sequence dimension. This reduces activation memory proportionally to the world size.

**Key mechanisms:**

1. **Input distribution**: At embedding layer, combine batch and sequence dimensions, then split across ranks
2. **Attention layers**: Need full sequence for attention computation → all-gather before QKV projection, reduce-scatter after output projection
3. **MLP layers**: Can operate on local sequence chunks → all-gather before FC1, reduce-scatter after FC2
4. **Gradient synchronization**: During backward, gradients are automatically reduced across ranks

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Memory Layout with Sequence Parallelism"
        Input["Input IDs<br/>(batch, seqlen)"]
        Combine["Combine dimensions<br/>(batch*seqlen,)"]
        Split["Split across ranks<br/>(batch*seqlen/world_size,)"]
        Embed["Embedding<br/>(batch*seqlen/world_size, hidden_dim)"]
        
        Input --> Combine
        Combine --> Split
        Split --> Embed
    end
    
    subgraph "Attention Layer Flow"
        AG1["all_gather<br/>→ (batch*seqlen, hidden_dim)"]
        QKV["QKV Projection<br/>ColumnParallelLinear"]
        Attn["FlashAttention<br/>(requires seqlen)"]
        OutProj["Out Projection<br/>RowParallelLinear"]
        RS1["reduce_scatter<br/>→ (batch*seqlen/world_size, hidden_dim)"]
        
        Embed --> AG1
        AG1 --> QKV
        QKV --> Attn
        Attn --> OutProj
        OutProj --> RS1
    end
```

**Configuration in models:**

```python
# From create_mixer_cls and create_mlp_cls
parallel_kwargs = {
    "process_group": process_group,
    "sequence_parallel": getattr(config, "sequence_parallel", True),
}
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:90-97](), [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:514-532]()

## ParallelMHA

`ParallelMHA` implements multi-head attention with tensor parallelism. It differs from `MHA` by using `ColumnParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinear` for projections.

### Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ParallelMHA Forward Pass"
        Input["x<br/>(batch*seqlen/world_size, embed_dim)"]
        
        subgraph "QKV Projection - Column Parallel"
            AG_QKV["all_gather<br/>(if sequence_parallel)"]
            Wqkv["Wqkv: ColumnParallelLinear<br/>embed_dim → local_qkv_dim"]
            LocalQKV["qkv<br/>(batch*seqlen, 3, local_heads, head_dim)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Attention Computation"
            Rotary["RotaryEmbedding<br/>(if rotary_emb_dim > 0)"]
            FlashAttn["FlashSelfAttention<br/>(local heads only)"]
            Context["context<br/>(batch*seqlen, local_heads, head_dim)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Output Projection - Row Parallel"
            OutProj["out_proj: RowParallelLinear<br/>embed_dim → embed_dim"]
            RS_Out["reduce_scatter<br/>(if sequence_parallel)"]
            Output["output<br/>(batch*seqlen/world_size, embed_dim)"]
        end
        
        Input --> AG_QKV
        AG_QKV --> Wqkv
        Wqkv --> LocalQKV
        LocalQKV --> Rotary
        Rotary --> FlashAttn
        FlashAttn --> Context
        Context --> OutProj
        OutProj --> RS_Out
        RS_Out --> Output
    end
```

### Head Distribution

`ParallelMHA` distributes attention heads across ranks using `get_dim_for_local_rank()`, which handles uneven splits:

```python
# Each rank computes local_heads attention heads
self.local_num_heads = get_dim_for_local_rank(
    self.num_heads, self.world_size, self.local_rank
)
self.local_num_heads_kv = get_dim_for_local_rank(
    self.num_heads_kv, self.world_size, self.local_rank
)
```

For example, with 40 heads and 6 GPUs:
- Ranks 0-3: 7 heads each
- Ranks 4-5: 6 heads each

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:707-810]()

### Sequence Dimension Handling

When `sequence_parallel=True`, attention layers need the full sequence dimension for QK^T computation. The layer receives input as `(batch*seqlen/world_size, embed_dim)` but must pass `seqlen` to the attention kernel:

```python
# Forward pass in ParallelMHA
if self.sequence_parallel:
    kwargs["seqlen"] = seqlen  # Original full seqlen before split
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:848-861]()

## Parallel MLP Modules

### ParallelMLP

`ParallelMLP` implements a standard two-layer MLP with tensor parallelism:

```mermaid
graph LR
    X["x"] --> FC1["fc1: ColumnParallelLinear<br/>(all_gather if SP)"]
    FC1 --> Act["activation<br/>(gelu/relu/etc)"]
    Act --> FC2["fc2: RowParallelLinear<br/>(reduce_scatter if SP)"]
    FC2 --> Out["output"]
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/mlp.py:54-96]()

### ParallelFusedMLP

`ParallelFusedMLP` uses fused kernels that combine linear + activation into a single CUDA kernel for better performance:

```python
# Uses FusedMLPFunc which combines:
# 1. All-gather (if sequence_parallel)
# 2. Linear + activation (fc1 + gelu/relu in one kernel)
# 3. Linear (fc2)
# 4. Reduce-scatter (if sequence_parallel)
```

The fused implementation supports checkpoint levels for trading off memory vs computation:
- `checkpoint_lvl=0`: Save all intermediate activations
- `checkpoint_lvl=1`: Recompute activation output in backward
- `checkpoint_lvl=2`: Recompute both pre-activation and activation output in backward

**Sources:** [flash_attn/ops/fused_dense.py:613-688]()

### ParallelGatedMlp

`ParallelGatedMlp` implements gated activations (GLU, SwiGLU, GeGLU) with tensor parallelism:

```mermaid
graph TB
    X["x"] --> FC1["fc1: ColumnParallelLinear<br/>output: 2*hidden_features"]
    FC1 --> Split["chunk(2, dim=-1)"]
    Split --> Y["y"]
    Split --> Gate["gate"]
    Gate --> ActFn["activation(gate)"]
    Y --> Mul["y * activation(gate)"]
    ActFn --> Mul
    Mul --> FC2["fc2: RowParallelLinear"]
    FC2 --> Out["output"]
```

The `fc1` layer outputs `2*hidden_features`, which is split into two halves. The gate half goes through the activation function before being multiplied with the other half.

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/mlp.py:139-191]()

## ParallelBlock

`ParallelBlock` is a transformer block where attention and MLP are computed in parallel (as in GPT-J, GPT-NeoX, PaLM):

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ParallelBlock Structure"
        Input["hidden_states1, hidden_states2, residual"]
        
        subgraph "Dropout + Add + Norm"
            Drop1["dropout(hidden_states1)"]
            Drop2["dropout(hidden_states2)<br/>(if not first layer)"]
            Add["residual + dropped1 + dropped2"]
            Norm1["norm1(residual)"]
            Norm2["norm2(residual)<br/>(or norm1 if tied_norm)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Parallel Computation"
            Mixer["mixer (ParallelMHA)<br/>on norm1 output"]
            MLP["mlp (ParallelMLP)<br/>on norm2 output"]
        end
        
        Output["hidden_states1, hidden_states2, residual"]
        
        Input --> Drop1
        Input --> Drop2
        Drop1 --> Add
        Drop2 --> Add
        Add --> Norm1
        Add --> Norm2
        Norm1 --> Mixer
        Norm2 --> MLP
        Mixer --> Output
        MLP --> Output
        Add --> Output
    end
```

The key feature is that attention and MLP operate on the same input (after layernorm) rather than sequentially. This requires two separate outputs (`hidden_states1` for attention, `hidden_states2` for MLP) that are both added to the residual in the next block.

**Configuration:**
```python
# Enable parallel block in model config
config.parallel_block = True

# Optionally tie the two norms to save parameters
config.parallel_block_tied_norm = True
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/block.py:259-397](), [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:277-306]()

## State Dict Sharding

When loading pretrained models with tensor parallelism, weights must be sharded appropriately across ranks.

### shard_state_dict_tp

`shard_state_dict_tp()` transforms a standard state dict into a tensor-parallel state dict for a specific rank:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "State Dict Sharding Operations"
        FullSD["Full State Dict<br/>(from pretrained model)"]
        
        subgraph "Embeddings"
            WordEmbed["word_embeddings.weight<br/>shard on dim 0 (vocab)"]
            PosEmbed["position_embeddings.weight<br/>shard on dim 1"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Attention Layers"
            QKV["Wqkv.weight/bias<br/>shard by heads"]
            OutProj["out_proj.weight<br/>shard on dim 1<br/>(multiple_of=head_dim)"]
            OutBias["out_proj.bias<br/>(rank 0 only)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "MLP Layers"
            FC1["fc1.weight/bias<br/>shard on dim 0"]
            FC1Gate["fc1 (gated)<br/>special gated sharding"]
            FC2["fc2.weight<br/>shard on dim 1"]
            FC2Bias["fc2.bias<br/>(rank 0 only)"]
        end
        
        subgraph "LM Head"
            LMHead["lm_head.weight<br/>shard on dim 0 (vocab)"]
        end
        
        FullSD --> WordEmbed
        FullSD --> PosEmbed
        FullSD --> QKV
        FullSD --> OutProj
        FullSD --> FC1
        FullSD --> FC2
        FullSD --> LMHead
    end
```

**Key sharding strategies:**

| Component | Sharding Strategy | Notes |
|-----------|-------------------|-------|
| `word_embeddings.weight` | `shard_first_dim` | Vocabulary partitioned across ranks |
| `position_embeddings.weight` | `shard_last_dim` | Hidden dim partitioned |
| `Wqkv.weight/bias` | `shard_qkv_headdim` | Handles GQA/MQA by partitioning Q, K, V heads separately |
| `out_proj.weight` | `shard_last_dim(multiple_of=head_dim)` | Ensures alignment with head boundaries |
| `out_proj.bias` | Kept on rank 0 only | Removed from other ranks to avoid duplicate addition |
| `fc1.weight/bias` | `shard_first_dim` (or `shard_gatedmlp_fc1_dim` for gated) | Output dim partitioned |
| `fc2.weight` | `shard_last_dim` | Input dim partitioned |
| `fc2.bias` | Kept on rank 0 only | Removed from other ranks |

**GQA/MQA head sharding:**

For Grouped Query Attention where `num_heads_kv < num_heads`, the QKV tensor is laid out as:
```
[Q_heads | K_heads | V_heads]
```

`shard_qkv_headdim()` partitions Q heads differently from K/V heads:
```python
# Different number of Q and KV heads per rank
n_head_each_rank = [get_dim_for_local_rank(n_head, world_size, r) for r in range(world_size)]
n_head_kv_each_rank = [get_dim_for_local_rank(n_head_kv, world_size, r) for r in range(world_size)]

# Extract appropriate slices for this rank
qkv_local = torch.cat([
    qkv[beg_n_head:end_n_head],           # Q heads for this rank
    qkv[n_head+beg_n_head_kv:n_head+end_n_head_kv],     # K heads
    qkv[n_head+n_head_kv+beg_n_head_kv:n_head+n_head_kv+end_n_head_kv]  # V heads
], dim=0)
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:698-811]()

### combine_state_dicts_tp

`combine_state_dicts_tp()` is the inverse operation, combining tensor-parallel state dicts from all ranks back into a standard state dict:

```python
def combine_state_dicts_tp(state_dicts: List[Dict[str, torch.Tensor]], config: GPT2Config):
    """Convert list of sharded state_dicts to standard state_dict.
    
    Precondition: state_dicts ordered same as shards were created.
    """
    # Combine word embeddings (can be sharded on dim 0 or 1)
    state_dict['word_embeddings.weight'] = torch.cat([s['word_embeddings.weight'] for s in state_dicts], dim=...)
    
    # Combine QKV heads
    state_dict['Wqkv.weight'] = combine_qkv_headdim(state_dicts, key)
    
    # Combine other weights by concatenating along sharded dimension
    ...
```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:814-896]()

## Communication Primitives

Tensor parallelism relies on collective communication operations from `flash_attn.utils.distributed`:

### all_gather and all_gather_raw

Gather tensors from all ranks along a specified dimension:

```python
# all_gather: Friendly wrapper
output = all_gather(tensor, process_group, dim=0)

# all_gather_raw: Low-level with async support
output, handle = all_gather_raw(tensor, process_group, async_op=True)
handle.wait()  # Synchronize when needed
```

Used in:
- Sequence parallel: Gather sequence dimension before attention/MLP
- Column parallel: Gather input before matmul (when sequence_parallel=True)

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/distributed.py]()

### reduce_scatter and reduce_scatter_raw

Reduce tensors from all ranks (sum) then scatter the result:

```python
# reduce_scatter: Friendly wrapper
output = reduce_scatter(tensor, process_group, dim=0)

# reduce_scatter_raw: Low-level with async support
output, handle = reduce_scatter_raw(tensor, process_group, async_op=True)
```

Used in:
- Sequence parallel: Reduce-scatter after attention/MLP output
- Row parallel: Reduce gradients in backward pass

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/distributed.py]()

### all_reduce and all_reduce_raw

Reduce tensors from all ranks (sum) and replicate result to all ranks:

```python
# Used when sequence_parallel=False
output = all_reduce(tensor, process_group)
```

Used in:
- Non-sequence parallel mode: Reduce row-parallel outputs without scattering
- Norm parameters: All-reduce gradients for shared parameters

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/distributed.py]()

### sync_shared_params

Synchronize parameters marked with `_shared_params` attribute:

```python
# In GPTModel.__init__
if process_group is not None:
    for p in self.ln_f.parameters():
        p._shared_params = True  # Mark for synchronization
        if self.sequence_parallel:
            p._sequence_parallel = True  # All-reduce gradients
```

Called in `tie_weights()` to ensure all ranks start with identical norm parameters.

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:486-506](), [flash_attn/utils/distributed.py]()

## Usage Example

### Enabling Tensor Parallelism

```python
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from transformers import GPT2Config
from flash_attn.models.gpt import GPTLMHeadModel

# Initialize process group
dist.init_process_group(backend='nccl')
process_group = dist.new_group()  # or use default group
rank = dist.get_rank(process_group)
world_size = dist.get_world_size(process_group)

# Create config with tensor parallel settings
config = GPT2Config(
    vocab_size=50257,
    n_embd=2048,
    n_head=16,
    n_layer=24,
    sequence_parallel=True,  # Enable sequence parallelism
    fused_mlp=True,          # Use fused kernels for better perf
    use_flash_attn=True,     # Use FlashAttention
)

# Create model with tensor parallel support
model = GPTLMHeadModel(
    config, 
    process_group=process_group,
    device=f'cuda:{rank}',
    dtype=torch.bfloat16
)

# Load pretrained weights (automatically sharded)
model = GPTLMHeadModel.from_pretrained(
    'gpt2',
    config=config,
    world_size=world_size,
    rank=rank,
    device=f'cuda:{rank}',
    dtype=torch.bfloat16
)
```

### Forward Pass with Sequence Parallelism

```python
# Input: (batch_size, seqlen)
input_ids = torch.randint(0, 50257, (2, 1024), device=f'cuda:{rank}')

# With sequence_parallel=True, embeddings layer combines batch*seqlen
# and splits across ranks: (batch*seqlen/world_size, n_embd)
output = model(input_ids)

# output.logits shape: (batch, seqlen, vocab_size) on all ranks
# During inference, all-gather is performed to get full vocab logits
```

### Memory Benefits

For a model with:
- `batch_size=2`, `seqlen=2048`, `hidden_dim=4096`, `vocab_size=50257`
- `world_size=8`, `dtype=bfloat16` (2 bytes)

Without tensor/sequence parallelism (per GPU):
- Embeddings: `2 * 2048 * 4096 * 2 = 33.6 MB`
- Attention activations: `2 * 2048 * 4096 * 2 = 33.6 MB`
- MLP activations: `2 * 2048 * 4096 * 4 * 2 = 134.4 MB` (4x expansion)

With sequence parallelism (per GPU):
- Embeddings: `2 * 256 * 4096 * 2 = 4.2 MB` (8x reduction)
- Attention activations: `2 * 256 * 4096 * 2 = 4.2 MB` (8x reduction)
- MLP activations: `2 * 256 * 4096 * 4 * 2 = 16.8 MB` (8x reduction)

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:410-574](), [tests/modules/test_mlp_parallel.py:24-103]()

## Parameter Marking and Gradient Synchronization

Tensor parallelism requires special handling for certain parameters:

### Shared Parameters

Parameters replicated across ranks (e.g., LayerNorm) are marked with `_shared_params`:

```python
# In Block and ParallelBlock
if mark_shared_params:
    for p in self.norm1.parameters():
        p._shared_params = True
```

These parameters are synchronized at initialization via `sync_shared_params()` to ensure all ranks start with identical values.

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/block.py:98-103]()

### Sequence Parallel Gradients

Parameters in sequence-parallel layers are marked with `_sequence_parallel`:

```python
if sequence_parallel:
    for p in self.norm1.parameters():
        p._sequence_parallel = True
```

This signals that gradients should be all-reduced across ranks during backward pass, since each rank computed gradients on only a portion of the sequence.

**Sources:** [flash_attn/modules/block.py:91-96]()

### Optimizer Considerations

When using tensor parallelism, optimizers must account for:
1. Different learning rates for sharded parameters (optional, for μP scaling)
2. Gradient clipping should be computed after all-reduce
3. Parameter updates are local to each rank's shard

**Sources:** [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:380-407]()

# Text Generation and Inference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This page covers the text generation utilities in `flash_attn/utils/generation.py`, including the autoregressive decode loop, sampling strategies, KV cache state management, CUDA graph optimization, and speculative decoding. For the KV caching mechanism used inside the attention kernel itself, see [KV Caching Systems](#5.4). For the MHA module and how `InferenceParams` is consumed per layer, see [MHA Module](#7.1).

---

## Overview

The generation system is a self-contained stack in `flash_attn/utils/generation.py` that provides:

- A token-by-token autoregressive decoding loop (`decode`)
- Pluggable sampling strategies (greedy, top-k, top-p)
- A stateful KV cache object (`InferenceParams`) that accumulates key/value tensors across steps
- Optional CUDA graph capture to eliminate Python overhead during the decode phase
- A speculative decoding implementation (`decode_speculative`) using a draft model

Models that want to use this stack inherit from `GenerationMixin` (defined in `generation.py`) and implement `allocate_inference_cache`. The `GPTLMHeadModel` in `flash_attn/models/gpt.py` is the primary model that does this.

```
flash_attn/utils/generation.py   ← all generation primitives live here
flash_attn/modules/mha.py        ← consumes InferenceParams per layer
flash_attn/models/gpt.py         ← GPTLMHeadModel uses GenerationMixin
```

---

## Key Data Structures

### `InferenceParams`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:23-41]()

`InferenceParams` is a plain dataclass that holds all mutable state shared across a single generation run.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `max_seqlen` | `int` | Maximum sequence length allocated for KV cache |
| `max_batch_size` | `int` | Maximum batch size allocated |
| `seqlen_offset` | `int` | Number of tokens already processed; advances each step |
| `batch_size_offset` | `int` | Start index in the batch dimension; used for beam search |
| `key_value_memory_dict` | `dict[int, Tensor]` | Maps layer index → KV cache tensor `(B, max_seqlen, 2, nheads, headdim)` |
| `lengths_per_sample` | `Optional[Tensor]` | Per-sample KV lengths for variable-length batches |

The `reset(max_seqlen, max_batch_size)` method zeroes `seqlen_offset` and `lengths_per_sample` so the same allocated buffers can be reused for a new request (important for CUDA graph replay).

### `DecodingCGCache`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:605-614]()

Holds the CUDA graph state for the decode step.

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `callables` | `dict` mapping `(batch_size, seqlen)` → captured graph callable |
| `mempool` | Shared memory pool across all captured graphs |
| `inference_params` | The `InferenceParams` object whose buffers are baked into the graph |
| `run` | A callable that dispatches to the right graph based on current input shape |

## Generation API and Strategies

### `sample`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:69-95]()

The `sample` function takes a logits tensor of shape `(batch_size, vocab_size)` and returns a token index tensor of shape `(batch_size,)`.

| `top_k` value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `1` | Greedy decoding: returns `logits.argmax(dim=-1)` directly |
| `> 1` | Samples from top-k candidates; applies top-p filter if `top_p > 0` |
| `0` | Pure sampling over the full vocabulary (after optional top-p filter) |

Top-k and top-p can be combined: top-k is applied first, then top-p within the top-k set.

Helper functions applied in-place on logits:
- `modify_logits_for_top_k_filtering(logits, top_k)` — sets non-top-k logits to `-inf`
- `modify_logits_for_top_p_filtering(logits, top_p)` — sets cumulative-probability-tail logits to `-inf`

### `decode`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]()

The main generation loop. Decorated with `@torch.inference_mode()`.

**Signature:**
```python
decode(input_ids, model, max_length, top_k=1, top_p=0.0, temperature=1.0,
       eos_token_id=None, teacher_outputs=None, vocab_size=None,
       tensor_parallel=1, cg=False, enable_timing=False)
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `input_ids` | `(batch, seq_len)` — the prompt tokens |
| `model` | Any model with a `forward(input_ids, position_ids, inference_params, num_last_tokens)` interface |
| `max_length` | Total sequence length to generate (prompt + new tokens) |
| `cg` | If `True`, use CUDA graphs for the decode steps |
| `teacher_outputs` | If provided, forces next tokens from this tensor (for testing) |
| `vocab_size` | Truncates logits to this size (useful when vocab is padded) |
| `tensor_parallel` | Number of tensor-parallel ranks; used to synchronize timing barriers |

**Return value:** `GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput` or `SampleDecoderOnlyOutput` with fields:
- `sequences`: `(batch, max_length)` generated token ids
- `scores`: tuple of per-step logits `(batch, vocab_size)`

### `GenerationMixin`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:566-586]()

A mixin providing a `generate` method that delegates to `decode`. Subclasses must implement `allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype)`.

`GPTLMHeadModel` in `flash_attn/models/gpt.py` inherits both `GPTPreTrainedModel` and `GenerationMixin`, and forwards `allocate_inference_cache` calls to each transformer layer.

---

## Decode Loop Internals

**Token-by-token autoregressive decode flow**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as "caller"
    participant D as "decode()"
    participant M as "model.forward()"
    participant IP as "InferenceParams"
    participant S as "sample()"

    C->>D: "input_ids, max_length"
    D->>IP: "create / reset"
    loop "while not should_stop()"
        D->>M: "forward(tokens, position_ids, inference_params, num_last_tokens=1)"
        M-->>D: "logits (batch, vocab_size)"
        D->>IP: "seqlen_offset += seqlen"
        D->>S: "sample(logits, top_k, top_p, temperature)"
        S-->>D: "next_token (batch,)"
    end
    D-->>C: "sequences, scores"
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:145-206]()

Key observations:
- On the first step (`seqlen_offset == 0`), the full prompt is processed; subsequent steps process a single new token.
- `position_ids` is set to `seqlen_offset` during decoding steps so the model knows its absolute position.
- The `model.forward` is called with `num_last_tokens=1`, so only the logit for the final token position is computed and returned.
- Stopping conditions: `eos_token_id` encountered in all sequences, or `seqlen_offset >= max_length - 1`.

---

## InferenceParams and KV Cache State

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:23-41](), [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370]()

Each `MHA` layer reads and writes `InferenceParams.key_value_memory_dict[layer_idx]` to persist KV activations across generation steps.

### Cache allocation

Two allocation paths exist:

1. **Per-model allocation** — `GPTModel.allocate_inference_cache` delegates to each layer's `MHA.allocate_inference_cache`, which allocates a tensor of shape `(batch_size, max_seqlen, 2, num_heads_kv, head_dim)` and stores it in `inference_params.key_value_memory_dict`.

2. **Standalone utility** — `allocate_inference_cache(max_batch_size, max_seqlen, nheads, headdim, layers, device, dtype)` at [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:589-602]() creates the same structure without requiring a model instance.

### KV cache update in MHA

[flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370]()

The module-level `_update_kv_cache(kv, inference_params, layer_idx)` writes new KV tensors into the pre-allocated buffer using `seqlen_offset` as the write position and returns a slice up to the current position for use in attention.

For the fast path when `seqlen_offset > 0` and `use_flash_attn` is enabled, `MHA._apply_rotary_update_kvcache_attention` [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:502-540]() fuses rotary application, KV cache write, and attention into a single `flash_attn_with_kvcache` call.

---

## CUDA Graph Optimization

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-700]()

CUDA graphs allow the GPU work for a fixed-shape decode step to be recorded once and replayed with zero Python overhead.

### `update_graph_cache`

**Signature:**
```python
update_graph_cache(model, cache, batch_size, seqlen_og, max_seqlen,
                   decoding_seqlens=(1,), tensor_parallel=1,
                   dtype=None, n_warmups=2)
```

The function:
1. Allocates `InferenceParams` with `max_seqlen` and `max_batch_size = batch_size`.
2. Calls `model.allocate_inference_cache` so the KV buffers are created and baked into the graph.
3. For each `seqlen` in `decoding_seqlens`, performs `n_warmups` warmup runs, then captures a CUDA graph using `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph`.
4. Returns a populated `DecodingCGCache` whose `run` method selects the correct graph by `(batch_size, seqlen)` and replays it.

**When to call it:** Call `update_graph_cache` before the generation loop starts. Pass `cg=True` to `decode` or `decode_speculative` to activate graph replay.

**Constraints for CUDA graph compatibility:**
- Tensor shapes must be static (same batch size and sequence length per replay).
- Input/output tensors must remain at fixed memory addresses (the graph captures pointer values).
- The model must not branch on dynamic conditions inside the captured region.

**Diagram: CUDA graph capture and replay**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Capture phase (update_graph_cache)"
        W["warmup runs\n(n_warmups=2)"]
        CAP["torch.cuda.CUDAGraph.capture_begin/end"]
        STORE["DecodingCGCache.callables[batch,seqlen]"]
        W --> CAP --> STORE
    end
    subgraph "Replay phase (decode loop)"
        RUN["DecodingCGCache.run(input_ids, position_ids, seqlen_offset)"]
        REPLAY["graph.replay()"]
        OUT["static output buffer"]
        RUN --> REPLAY --> OUT
    end
    STORE --> RUN
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-700]()

---

## Speculative Decoding

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-563]()

Speculative decoding uses a small *draft model* to propose `speculative_lookahead` candidate tokens, which are then verified in a single forward pass of the larger *main model*.

### `decode_speculative`

**Signature:**
```python
decode_speculative(input_ids, model, model_draft, max_length,
                   speculative_lookahead=3, top_k=1, top_p=0.0,
                   temperature=1.0, eos_token_id=None, vocab_size=None,
                   tensor_parallel=1, cg=False, enable_timing=False, debug=False)
```

**Limitations (current implementation):**
- `batch_size` must be 1
- `eos_token_id` is not supported

### `sample_speculative`

[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:209-265]()

Implements Algorithm 1 from the speculative decoding paper (Leviathan et al., 2022).

**Inputs:**

| Argument | Shape | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `logits` | `(batch, seqlen+1, vocab)` | Main model logits for all draft + 1 bonus position |
| `logits_draft` | `(batch, seqlen, vocab)` | Draft model logits for draft tokens |
| `tokens_draft` | `(batch, seqlen)` | Tokens proposed by the draft model |

**Output:**
- `tokens`: `(batch, seqlen+1)` — the accepted tokens plus one resampled token
- `num_generated_tokens`: `(batch,)` — number of valid tokens per sequence (in `[1, seqlen+1]`)

The acceptance criterion per draft token `t`: accept with probability `min(1, p_main(t) / p_draft(t))`. If a token is rejected, resample from the residual distribution `max(0, p_main - p_draft)`.

### Speculative decode loop

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant L as "decode_speculative()"
    participant D as "model_draft"
    participant M as "model"
    participant SS as "sample_speculative()"

    L->>D: "sample n_spec_tokens tokens autoregressively"
    D-->>L: "tokens_draft, scores_draft"
    L->>M: "forward(concat(last_token, tokens_draft), num_last_tokens=n+1)"
    M-->>L: "logits (batch, n+1, vocab)"
    L->>SS: "sample_speculative(logits, scores_draft, tokens_draft)"
    SS-->>L: "accepted_tokens, num_generated"
    L->>L: "advance seqlen_offset by num_generated"
    L->>L: "repeat until max_length"
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:373-563]()

### `forward` with `inference_params`

[flash_attn/models/gpt.py:635-669]()

`GPTLMHeadModel.forward` accepts `inference_params` and `num_last_tokens`. When `num_last_tokens > 0`, only the last `num_last_tokens` hidden states are projected to logits, which avoids recomputing logits for tokens already committed to the KV cache.

During tensor-parallel inference, `all_gather_raw` collects partial logits from all ranks before returning.

This page documents the text generation API and sampling strategies implemented in FlashAttention's model integration layer. The generation utilities enable autoregressive token generation with various decoding strategies (greedy, top-k, top-p sampling) and performance optimizations (CUDA graphs, speculative decoding).

For KV cache management during generation, see [InferenceParams and KV Cache State](#12.2). For CUDA graph optimization details, see [CUDA Graph Optimization](#12.3). For speculative decoding internals, see [Speculative Decoding](#12.4).

## Generation API Overview

The generation API provides two main entry points: `decode()` for standard generation and `decode_speculative()` for speculative decoding with a draft model. Models can also expose a `generate()` method via the `GenerationMixin` class.

```mermaid

    style Decode fill:#ffe1e1

```

**Figure: Generation API Architecture**

The `decode()` function orchestrates the generation loop: it repeatedly calls the model to get logits, applies sampling to select tokens, and manages KV cache state via `InferenceParams`. The `GenerationMixin` class provides a convenient wrapper compatible with HuggingFace's generation API.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:24-206](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:566-586]()

## Main Generation Functions

### decode()

The primary generation function supports both greedy decoding and sampling-based generation with configurable stopping criteria.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `input_ids` | `Tensor` | Input token IDs of shape `(batch, seq_len)` |
| `model` | `nn.Module` | Model to generate from (must accept `inference_params`) |
| `max_length` | `int` | Maximum sequence length to generate |
| `top_k` | `int` | Number of top tokens to consider (1 = greedy, 0 = no limit) |
| `top_p` | `float` | Cumulative probability threshold for nucleus sampling |
| `temperature` | `float` | Temperature for softmax (higher = more random) |
| `eos_token_id` | `Optional[int]` | Token ID that signals end of sequence |
| `teacher_outputs` | `Optional[Tensor]` | If provided, use these tokens instead of sampling (for testing) |
| `vocab_size` | `Optional[int]` | Vocabulary size (used to slice logits in tensor parallel mode) |
| `tensor_parallel` | `int` | Number of GPUs for tensor parallelism |
| `cg` | `bool` | Whether to use CUDA graphs for optimization |
| `enable_timing` | `bool` | Whether to measure and print timing statistics |

**Returns**: `GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput` or `SampleDecoderOnlyOutput` with fields:
- `sequences`: Generated token sequences of shape `(batch, max_length)`
- `scores`: Tuple of logits at each generation step, each of shape `(batch, vocab_size)`

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["decode() called"]
    InitCache["Initialize InferenceParams<br/>or use cached CUDA graph"]
    Loop["Generation loop"]
    GetLogits["get_logits():<br/>model(input_ids, inference_params)"]
    CheckStop{"should_stop()?<br/>EOS or max_length?"}
    SampleTokens["sample_tokens():<br/>sample(logits, top_k, top_p, temp)"]
    UpdateOffset["inference_params.seqlen_offset += 1"]
    AppendSeq["Append token to sequences"]
    Return["Return Output with<br/>sequences and scores"]
    
    Start --> InitCache
    InitCache --> Loop
    Loop --> GetLogits
    GetLogits --> CheckStop
    CheckStop -->|No| SampleTokens
    SampleTokens --> UpdateOffset
    UpdateOffset --> AppendSeq
    AppendSeq --> Loop
    CheckStop -->|Yes| Return
    
    style GetLogits fill:#ffe1e1
    style SampleTokens fill:#e1ffe1
    style UpdateOffset fill:#e1f5ff
```

**Figure: decode() Generation Loop**

The generation loop has three phases:
1. **Prefill**: Process the initial `input_ids` (all tokens at once) when `seqlen_offset == 0`
2. **Decode**: Generate one token at a time, updating `seqlen_offset` after each step
3. **Termination**: Stop when EOS token is generated or `max_length` is reached

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]()

### CUDA Graph Mode

When `cg=True`, the decode function uses CUDA graphs to eliminate kernel launch overhead. The graph is captured once per `(batch_size, decoding_seqlen)` combination and replayed for each generation step.

```python
# Pseudo-code showing CUDA graph usage
if cg:
    # Capture graphs for this batch size and max_length
    model._decoding_cache = update_graph_cache(
        model, model._decoding_cache, batch_size, seqlen_og, max_length
    )
    inference_params = model._decoding_cache.inference_params
    
    # During decoding, use cached graph
    logits = model._decoding_cache.run(
        input_ids, position_ids, inference_params.seqlen_offset
    )
```

The `update_graph_cache()` function manages a cache of captured graphs indexed by `(batch_size, decoding_seqlen)`. This allows handling variable batch sizes and sequence lengths without re-capturing graphs.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:130-167](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-690]()

## Sampling Strategies

The `sample()` function implements three sampling strategies that can be combined:

### Strategy Comparison

| Strategy | `top_k` | `top_p` | `temperature` | Behavior |
|----------|---------|---------|---------------|----------|
| **Greedy** | 1 | any | any | Select argmax token (deterministic) |
| **Top-k** | k > 1 | 0.0 | T | Sample from k highest probability tokens |
| **Nucleus (top-p)** | 0 | p ∈ (0,1] | T | Sample from smallest set with cumulative prob ≥ p |
| **Top-k + Nucleus** | k > 1 | p ∈ (0,1] | T | Apply top-k first, then nucleus |
| **Pure Sampling** | 0 | 0.0 | T | Sample from all tokens (temperature scaling only) |

### sample() Implementation Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["sample(logits, top_k, top_p, temperature)"]
    CheckGreedy{"top_k == 1?"}
    Argmax["return logits.argmax(dim=-1)"]
    
    CheckTopK{"top_k > 0?"}
    ApplyTopK["Extract top_k logits and indices"]
    ScaleTemp1["logits /= temperature"]
    ApplyTopP1["modify_logits_for_top_p_filtering()"]
    Multinomial1["multinomial(softmax(logits))"]
    ReturnIdx1["Return indices[sampled]"]
    
    CloneLogits["logits = logits / temperature"]
    ApplyTopP2["modify_logits_for_top_p_filtering()"]
    Multinomial2["multinomial(softmax(logits))"]
    
    Input --> CheckGreedy
    CheckGreedy -->|Yes| Argmax
    CheckGreedy -->|No| CheckTopK
    
    CheckTopK -->|Yes| ApplyTopK
    ApplyTopK --> ScaleTemp1
    ScaleTemp1 --> ApplyTopP1
    ApplyTopP1 --> Multinomial1
    Multinomial1 --> ReturnIdx1
    
    CheckTopK -->|No| CloneLogits
    CloneLogits --> ApplyTopP2
    ApplyTopP2 --> Multinomial2
    
    style Argmax fill:#e1ffe1
    style ApplyTopK fill:#ffe1e1
    style ApplyTopP1 fill:#fff4e1
    style ApplyTopP2 fill:#fff4e1
```

**Figure: sample() Decision Tree**

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:69-95]()

### Top-k Filtering

The `modify_logits_for_top_k_filtering()` function masks out all tokens except the top-k highest probability tokens by setting their logits to `-inf`:

```python
def modify_logits_for_top_k_filtering(logits, top_k):
    """Set the logits for none top-k values to -inf. Done in-place."""
    indices_to_remove = logits < torch.topk(logits, top_k)[0][..., -1, None]
    logits.masked_fill_(indices_to_remove, float("-Inf"))
```

This is efficient because it operates in-place on the logits tensor and uses `torch.topk()` which is optimized for GPU.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:45-48]()

### Top-p (Nucleus) Filtering

The `modify_logits_for_top_p_filtering()` function implements nucleus sampling by:
1. Sorting logits in descending order
2. Computing cumulative probabilities after softmax
3. Removing tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds `1 - top_p`

```python
def modify_logits_for_top_p_filtering(logits, top_p):
    """Set the logits for none top-p values to -inf. Done in-place."""
    if top_p <= 0.0 or top_p >= 1.0:
        return
    # Sort and calculate cumulative sum of probabilities
    sorted_logits, sorted_indices = torch.sort(logits, descending=False)
    cumulative_probs = sorted_logits.softmax(dim=-1).cumsum(dim=-1)
    # Remove tokens with cumulative top_p above threshold
    sorted_indices_to_remove = cumulative_probs <= (1 - top_p)
    # Scatter back to original indexing
    indices_to_remove = sorted_indices_to_remove.scatter(
        1, sorted_indices, sorted_indices_to_remove
    )
    logits.masked_fill_(indices_to_remove, float("-inf"))
```

The algorithm sorts in **ascending** order to correctly identify tokens that should be **kept** (cumulative probability from the top). The scatter operation is necessary to map the sorted indices back to the original token indices.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:53-66]()

### Temperature Scaling

Temperature controls the "randomness" of sampling by scaling logits before applying softmax:

- `temperature = 1.0`: No scaling (default behavior)
- `temperature < 1.0`: Sharper distribution (more deterministic, "less creative")
- `temperature > 1.0`: Flatter distribution (more random, "more creative")

The scaling is applied as `logits /= temperature` before computing softmax probabilities. Lower temperature makes high-probability tokens even more likely, while higher temperature increases the probability of lower-ranked tokens.

## Speculative Decoding

Speculative decoding uses a smaller "draft" model to propose multiple tokens in parallel, which are then verified by the main model in a single forward pass. This can achieve 1.5-2× speedups for generation-heavy workloads.

### Algorithm Overview

The `sample_speculative()` function implements Algorithm 1 from ["Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192) (Leviathan et al., 2022):

```mermaid
graph TD
    DraftModel["Draft model generates<br/>n tokens: x₁, x₂, ..., xₙ"]
    MainModel["Main model evaluates<br/>all n+1 positions in parallel"]
    
    subgraph "Rejection Sampling Loop"
        CheckToken["For each position i"]
        CalcProb["p_main = main_model_prob[xᵢ]<br/>p_draft = draft_model_prob[xᵢ]"]
        AcceptTest{"random() * p_draft<br/>≤ p_main?"}
        Accept["Accept token xᵢ"]
        Reject["Reject at position i"]
        Resample["Resample from<br/>p_adjusted = max(0, p_main - p_draft)"]
    end
    
    ReturnTokens["Return accepted tokens<br/>+ resampled token"]
    
    DraftModel --> MainModel
    MainModel --> CheckToken
    CheckToken --> CalcProb
    CalcProb --> AcceptTest
    AcceptTest -->|Yes| Accept
    AcceptTest -->|No| Reject
    Accept --> CheckToken
    Reject --> Resample
    Resample --> ReturnTokens
    
    style DraftModel fill:#ffe1e1
    style MainModel fill:#fff4e1
    style Resample fill:#e1ffe1
```

**Figure: Speculative Decoding Rejection Sampling**

### sample_speculative() Implementation

The function takes logits from both models and the draft tokens, then performs rejection sampling:

| Parameter | Shape | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `logits` | `(batch, seqlen+1, vocab_size)` | Main model logits for all positions |
| `logits_draft` | `(batch, seqlen, vocab_size)` | Draft model logits (excluding last position) |
| `tokens_draft` | `(batch, seqlen)` | Tokens proposed by draft model |
| `top_k`, `top_p`, `temperature` | Scalars | Sampling parameters |

**Returns**:
- `tokens`: Tensor of shape `(batch, seqlen+1)` with accepted/resampled tokens
- `num_generated_tokens`: Tensor of shape `(batch,)` with counts ∈ [1, seqlen+1]

The key insight is that the main model produces `seqlen+1` logits (one for each draft token plus one extra), allowing it to either accept all draft tokens and generate a new one, or reject at some position and resample.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:209-265]()

### decode_speculative() Loop

The `decode_speculative()` function coordinates the draft model and main model:

```python
# Simplified pseudo-code
while True:
    # Draft model generates n_spec_tokens
    tokens_draft, scores_draft = sample_tokens_draft(
        sequences[-1][:, -2:], num_tokens=n_spec_tokens
    )
    
    # Main model evaluates draft tokens + generates one more
    logits = get_logits_main(
        torch.cat([sequences[-1][:, -1:], tokens_draft], dim=1),
        inference_params,
        num_last_tokens=n_spec_tokens + 1
    )
    
    # Rejection sampling decides which tokens to accept
    tokens, num_generated_tokens = sample_speculative(
        logits, scores_draft, tokens_draft, top_k=top_k, top_p=top_p, temperature=temperature
    )
    
    # Update state based on how many tokens were accepted
    sequences.append(tokens[:, :num_generated_tokens[0]])
    inference_params.seqlen_offset += num_generated_tokens[0].item()
```

The draft model needs to handle 1 or 2 tokens at a time (hence `decoding_seqlens=(1, 2)` in CUDA graph setup), while the main model needs to handle 1 to `speculative_lookahead+1` tokens.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-563]()

## GenerationMixin Integration

Models can inherit from `GenerationMixin` to expose a HuggingFace-compatible `generate()` method:

```python
class GenerationMixin:
    def generate(
        self,
        input_ids,
        max_length,
        top_k=1,
        top_p=0.0,
        temperature=1.0,
        return_dict_in_generate=False,
        output_scores=False,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        output = decode(
            input_ids, self, max_length, top_k=top_k, top_p=top_p, temperature=temperature, **kwargs
        )
        if not output_scores:
            output.scores = None
        return output if return_dict_in_generate else output.sequences
```

This allows models to be used with the same interface as HuggingFace models:

```python
# Both work the same way
output = model.generate(input_ids, max_length=100, top_k=50, temperature=0.8)
output = decode(input_ids, model, max_length=100, top_k=50, temperature=0.8)
```

Models must implement `allocate_inference_cache()` to support the mixin, which creates KV cache tensors for all layers.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:566-586](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:589-602]()

## Output Classes

The generation functions return either `GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput` (when `top_k=1`) or `SampleDecoderOnlyOutput` (when sampling):

```python
# From transformers, or defined as namedtuples if not installed
GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput = namedtuple("GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput", ["sequences", "scores"])
SampleDecoderOnlyOutput = namedtuple("SampleDecoderOnlyOutput", ["sequences", "scores"])
```

Both have identical structure:
- **`sequences`**: `Tensor` of shape `(batch, max_length)` containing generated token IDs
- **`scores`**: `tuple` of `Tensor`, each of shape `(batch, vocab_size)`, containing logits at each generation step

The `scores` field can be used to analyze the model's confidence or to implement custom sampling strategies.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:16-20](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:205-206]()

## Purpose and Scope

This page describes the `InferenceParams` data structure, how KV caches are allocated and managed during autoregressive text generation, and how state is updated step-by-step as new tokens are decoded. It covers the Python-level KV cache management used by the model integration layer.

For information about the low-level kernel-level KV cache write path (paged attention, `flash_attn_with_kvcache`), see [KV Caching Systems](#5.4). For information on the generation loop itself and sampling strategies, see [Generation API and Strategies](#8.1). For CUDA graph capture and replay using this state, see [CUDA Graph Optimization](#8.3).

---

## InferenceParams Data Structure

`InferenceParams` is a plain dataclass defined in [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:24-40]() that carries all mutable state the model needs during inference.

| Field | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_seqlen` | `int` | (required) | Maximum sequence length the KV cache was allocated for |
| `max_batch_size` | `int` | (required) | Maximum batch size the KV cache was allocated for |
| `seqlen_offset` | `int` | `0` | How many tokens have already been processed; indexes the write position in the KV cache |
| `batch_size_offset` | `int` | `0` | Starting row offset into the KV cache; used by beam search to select a sub-batch |
| `key_value_memory_dict` | `dict` | `{}` | Maps `layer_idx` → pre-allocated KV cache tensor for that layer |
| `lengths_per_sample` | `Optional[Tensor]` | `None` | Per-sample actual lengths, used when sequences in the batch have different lengths |

The `reset(max_seqlen, max_batch_size)` method [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:35-40]() resets `seqlen_offset` to `0` and zeroes `lengths_per_sample`. It does not reallocate memory, making it suitable for CUDA graph replay.

**Data structure and relationships:**

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class InferenceParams {
        +int max_seqlen
        +int max_batch_size
        +int seqlen_offset
        +int batch_size_offset
        +dict key_value_memory_dict
        +Optional[Tensor] lengths_per_sample
        +reset(max_seqlen, max_batch_size)
    }
    class KVCacheTensor {
        "shape: (max_batch_size, max_seqlen, 2, num_heads_kv, head_dim)"
        "dtype: fp16 or bf16"
    }
    InferenceParams --> KVCacheTensor : "key_value_memory_dict[layer_idx]"
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:24-40]()

---

## KV Cache Allocation

Two levels of allocation exist: one at the full model level, and one at the individual attention layer level.

### Model-level: `GPTModel.allocate_inference_cache`

[flash_attn/models/gpt.py:508-512]() iterates over all transformer layers and calls each layer's `allocate_inference_cache`, collecting results in a dict keyed by layer index. The returned dict can be used directly as `InferenceParams.key_value_memory_dict`.

```python
# Returns {0: tensor, 1: tensor, ..., n-1: tensor}
cache = model.allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype=torch.float16)
```

### Layer-level: `MHA.allocate_inference_cache`

[flash_attn/modules/mha.py:483-494]() allocates a single tensor per attention layer with shape:

```
(batch_size, max_seqlen, 2, num_heads_kv, head_dim)
```

The `2` dimension holds K and V concatenated. `num_heads_kv` accounts for GQA/MQA configurations where the number of KV heads may differ from query heads.

**Allocation flow:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "caller" as Caller
    participant "GPTModel" as GPTModel
    participant "Block/layer" as Block
    participant "MHA" as MHA

    Caller->>GPTModel: "allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype)"
    loop "for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers)"
        GPTModel->>Block: "allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype)"
        Block->>MHA: "allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype)"
        MHA-->>Block: "Tensor(batch_size, max_seqlen, 2, num_heads_kv, head_dim)"
        Block-->>GPTModel: "Tensor"
    end
    GPTModel-->>Caller: "dict {layer_idx: kv_cache_tensor}"
```

Sources: [flash_attn/models/gpt.py:508-512](), [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:483-494]()

---

## KV Cache Update Mechanism

### `_update_kv_cache` (module-level function)

[flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370]() is the core write routine. It:

1. Lazily allocates a cache tensor the first time a `layer_idx` is seen (if the dict is empty, e.g., when not using `allocate_inference_cache` ahead of time).
2. Writes the new KV slice into the pre-allocated buffer using `seqlen_offset` and `batch_size_offset`.
3. Returns a view of the filled portion of the cache: `kv_cache[batch_start:batch_end, :sequence_end, ...]`.

```
kv_cache[batch_start:batch_end, seqlen_offset : seqlen_offset + new_seqlen, ...] = kv
return kv_cache[batch_start:batch_end, :seqlen_offset + new_seqlen, ...]
```

The return value is the full KV context from position `0` up through the current token — this is passed directly to `flash_attn_with_kvcache` or used as the key/value input to the attention kernel.

**Write pattern into KV cache buffer:**

```mermaid
block-beta
    columns 8
    block:cache["KV cache buffer (max_seqlen)"]
        t0["token 0"] t1["token 1"] t2["token 2"] t3["token 3"] t4["token 4"] t5["..."] t6["slot N-1"]
    end

    space:8

    A["seqlen_offset=0\n(prefill phase)"] --> t0
    B["seqlen_offset=3\n(decode step 3)"] --> t3
```

Sources: [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370]()

### `MHA._update_kv_cache` (method)

[flash_attn/modules/mha.py:496-]() is the instance method version. It delegates to the module-level `_update_kv_cache`, passing `self.layer_idx` as the key into `inference_params.key_value_memory_dict`.

---

## seqlen_offset: Tracking Position Through Generation

`seqlen_offset` is the single counter that tracks how far into the KV cache we have written. It serves two roles:

1. **Write offset**: In `_update_kv_cache`, new KV data is written starting at `sequence_start = inference_params.seqlen_offset`.
2. **Rotary embedding position**: The `RotaryEmbedding` module uses `seqlen_offset` as a positional offset so that newly computed Q and K are assigned the correct sinusoidal position in the combined context.

The `decode` function [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:195-198]() advances `seqlen_offset` after each forward pass:

```python
while not should_stop(sequences[-1], inference_params):
    scores.append(get_logits(sequences[-1], inference_params))
    inference_params.seqlen_offset += sequences[-1].shape[1]
    sequences.append(sample_tokens(scores[-1], inference_params))
```

During the **prefill phase** (`seqlen_offset == 0`), the full prompt is processed. During subsequent **decode steps**, `seqlen_offset` equals the number of tokens already processed, and `sequences[-1].shape[1] == 1` for single-token decoding.

The model uses `seqlen_offset > 0` to distinguish between prefill and decode:

```python
decoding = inference_params.seqlen_offset > 0
```
[flash_attn/utils/generation.py:147]()

**State transitions across a generation step:**

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> "Prefill": "InferenceParams(seqlen_offset=0)"
    "Prefill" --> "Decode step 1": "seqlen_offset += prompt_len"
    "Decode step 1" --> "Decode step 2": "seqlen_offset += 1"
    "Decode step 2" --> "Decode step N": "seqlen_offset += 1"
    "Decode step N" --> [*]: "EOS or max_length reached"
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]()

---

## batch_size_offset: Beam Search Support

`batch_size_offset` offsets the batch dimension of the KV cache. In beam search, multiple hypotheses may share the same pre-allocated buffer, with each beam occupying a contiguous row range:

```
kv_cache[batch_size_offset : batch_size_offset + active_batch_size, ...]
```

For standard decoding, `batch_size_offset = 0` (the default). For beam search with beam width `W`, you would create separate `InferenceParams` instances with `batch_size_offset = 0, W, 2W, ...` pointing into a shared `key_value_memory_dict`.

Sources: [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:362-363]()

---

## lengths_per_sample

`lengths_per_sample` is an optional `Tensor` of shape `(batch_size,)` that tracks per-sample actual sequence lengths. This supports batches where different sequences have reached different generation positions (e.g., due to early EOS).

When set, it is zeroed by `reset()` [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:39-40](). The actual use of `lengths_per_sample` in attention kernels is via the `seqused_k` parameter in `flash_attn_with_kvcache`, which limits how much of the KV cache each sequence attends over.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:33-40]()

---

## Integration with MHA Forward Pass

The `MHA` module receives `inference_params` as a keyword argument during its forward pass. The key actions performed in order:

1. Project input to Q, K, V.
2. Apply rotary embeddings using `seqlen_offset` as the position base.
3. Call `_update_kv_cache(kv, inference_params, self.layer_idx)` to append the new KV into the cache and retrieve the full context.
4. Run attention using `flash_attn_with_kvcache` with the full cached KV context.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["MHA.forward(x, inference_params)"] --> B["Project x → q, k, v"]
    B --> C["Apply RotaryEmbedding\n(seqlen_offset=inference_params.seqlen_offset)"]
    C --> D["_update_kv_cache(kv, inference_params, layer_idx)\n→ returns kv_cache[..., :seqlen_offset+new_len, ...]"]
    D --> E["flash_attn_with_kvcache(q, kv_cache, ...)"]
    E --> F["out_proj(context)"]
```

Sources: [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370](), [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:483-494]()

---

## Integration with the decode Loop

The `decode` function [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]() is the primary consumer of `InferenceParams`. The lifecycle:

1. **Create** `InferenceParams(max_seqlen=max_length, max_batch_size=batch_size)`.
2. **Prefill**: call `model(input_ids, inference_params=inference_params)`. All layers write their KV into `key_value_memory_dict`.
3. **Advance**: `inference_params.seqlen_offset += prompt_len`.
4. **Decode loop**: for each step, call `model(next_token, inference_params=inference_params)`. Each layer appends one token to the cache.
5. **Advance**: `inference_params.seqlen_offset += 1`.

When CUDA graphs are enabled (`cg=True`), the `InferenceParams` object is retrieved from `model._decoding_cache.inference_params` and reset via `inference_params.reset(max_length, batch_size)` before the generation loop begins [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:141-142](). The `reset()` call is safe to use with a CUDA-graph-captured forward pass because it does not reallocate memory — it only resets the scalar `seqlen_offset`.

**Full lifecycle of InferenceParams in decode:**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "decode()" as decode
    participant "InferenceParams" as IP
    participant "GPTLMHeadModel" as Model
    participant "_update_kv_cache" as KVUpdate

    decode->>IP: "InferenceParams(max_seqlen, max_batch_size)"
    decode->>Model: "model(prompt, inference_params=IP)"
    Model->>KVUpdate: "_update_kv_cache(kv, IP, layer_idx=0..N)"
    KVUpdate->>IP: "key_value_memory_dict[i] = kv_cache"
    Model-->>decode: "logits"
    decode->>IP: "seqlen_offset += prompt_len"

    loop "decode step"
        decode->>Model: "model(next_token, inference_params=IP)"
        Model->>KVUpdate: "_update_kv_cache(kv, IP, layer_idx=0..N)"
        KVUpdate-->>Model: "kv_cache[..., :seqlen_offset+1, ...]"
        Model-->>decode: "logits"
        decode->>IP: "seqlen_offset += 1"
    end
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206](), [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370]()

---

## KV Cache Tensor Layout

Each per-layer cache tensor has the layout:

```
(max_batch_size, max_seqlen, 2, num_heads_kv, head_dim)
```

| Dimension | Size | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `max_batch_size` | Batch axis; `batch_size_offset` selects the active sub-batch |
| 1 | `max_seqlen` | Sequence axis; written up to `seqlen_offset` |
| 2 | `2` | K (`dim=0`) and V (`dim=1`) packed together |
| 3 | `num_heads_kv` | KV head count (supports GQA/MQA) |
| 4 | `head_dim` | Per-head embedding dimension |

Only `kv_cache[:, :seqlen_offset, ...]` contains valid data at any point during decoding. The remainder of the buffer is uninitialized but pre-allocated to avoid dynamic memory allocation in the generation loop.

Sources: [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:344-370](), [flash_attn/modules/mha.py:483-494]()

---

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the CUDA graph optimization system used to accelerate text generation and inference in flash-attention. CUDA graphs eliminate per-kernel launch overhead by capturing and replaying sequences of GPU operations, providing significant speedups for autoregressive decoding where the same computation pattern repeats across tokens.

This page covers the graph capture mechanism, cache management, and integration with the generation pipeline. For the high-level generation API and sampling strategies, see page 8.1. For the `InferenceParams` structure and KV cache allocation, see page 8.2.

## Overview

CUDA graph optimization works by recording a sequence of CUDA kernel launches into a graph structure that can be replayed efficiently. During autoregressive text generation, the model performs identical operations for each new token (with different data), making it ideal for CUDA graph optimization.

The system captures graphs for different sequence lengths during decoding, stores them in a cache, and replays them when generating subsequent tokens. This eliminates the overhead of launching individual CUDA kernels and significantly reduces latency, especially for small batch sizes.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:605-733]()

## Key Components

### InferenceParams

The `InferenceParams` dataclass ([flash_attn/utils/generation.py:23-41]()) manages state during inference, tracking sequence offsets and KV cache locations. See page 8.2 for a full description. The fields relevant to CUDA graph operation are:

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `max_seqlen` | `int` | Maximum sequence length allocated for inference |
| `max_batch_size` | `int` | Maximum batch size allocated |
| `seqlen_offset` | `int` | Current position in sequence; updated after each token |
| `key_value_memory_dict` | `dict` | Maps layer index → KV cache tensor |
| `lengths_per_sample` | `Optional[Tensor]` | Per-sample lengths for variable-length batches |

The `reset` method reinitializes `seqlen_offset` and zeros `lengths_per_sample` for a new generation run without reallocating memory.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:23-41]()

### DecodingCGCache

The `DecodingCGCache` dataclass ([flash_attn/utils/generation.py:605-614]()) stores all captured CUDA graphs and their associated state for a given model.

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `max_batch_size` | `int` | Batch size the graphs were captured for |
| `max_seqlen` | `int` | Max sequence length the graphs were captured for |
| `callables` | `dict` | Maps `(batch_size, decoding_seqlen)` → captured graph object |
| `mempool` | graph pool handle | Shared memory pool across all captured graphs |
| `inference_params` | `InferenceParams` | Shared inference state reused by all graphs |
| `run` | `Callable` | Dispatcher that copies inputs, replays the correct graph, returns logits |

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:605-614]()
