## Graph Capture Process

The `update_graph_cache` function handles capturing CUDA graphs for different sequence lengths. It implements a sophisticated caching strategy that accounts for varying batch sizes and sequence lengths.

### Capture Flow Diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    start["update_graph_cache() called"]
    check_cache{"Cache exists?"}
    check_params{"Params changed?"}
    
    allocate_kv["Allocate KV cache<br/>via allocate_inference_cache()"]
    create_mempool["Create CUDA graph<br/>memory pool"]
    
    warmup["Run n_warmups iterations<br/>default: 2"]
    
    capture_loop_start["For each decoding_seqlen"]
    setup_input["Create static input_ids<br/>position_ids tensors"]
    begin_capture["graph.capture_begin()"]
    forward_pass["model.forward()<br/>with inference_params"]
    end_capture["graph.capture_end()"]
    store_callable["Store graph callable<br/>in cache.callables"]
    capture_loop_end{"More seqlens?"}
    
    create_run["Create run() wrapper<br/>selects graph by seqlen"]
    attach_run["Attach run to cache"]
    
    return_cache["Return cache"]
    
    start --> check_cache
    check_cache -->|"No or changed"| allocate_kv
    check_cache -->|"Yes, unchanged"| return_cache
    
    allocate_kv --> create_mempool
    create_mempool --> warmup
    warmup --> capture_loop_start
    
    capture_loop_start --> setup_input
    setup_input --> begin_capture
    begin_capture --> forward_pass
    forward_pass --> end_capture
    end_capture --> store_callable
    store_callable --> capture_loop_end
    
    capture_loop_end -->|"Yes"| capture_loop_start
    capture_loop_end -->|"No"| create_run
    
    create_run --> attach_run
    attach_run --> return_cache
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-733]()

### Key Steps in Graph Capture

**1. Cache Validation**: `update_graph_cache` inspects `cache.max_batch_size`, `cache.max_seqlen`, `cache.device`, and `cache.dtype` against current arguments. If any differ, existing captured graphs are discarded and regenerated. An existing `DecodingCGCache` is reused when its parameters match.

**2. KV Cache Allocation**: A fresh `InferenceParams` is constructed with `max_batch_size=batch_size` and `max_seqlen=max_seqlen`. Its `key_value_memory_dict` is populated by calling `model.allocate_inference_cache(batch_size, max_seqlen, dtype=dtype)`, which pre-allocates layer-indexed KV cache tensors that persist for the lifetime of the cache.

**3. Memory Pool Creation**: A shared CUDA graph memory pool is created via `torch.cuda.graphs.graph_pool_handle()` and stored in `cache.mempool`. All graphs for the same model share this pool to reduce memory fragmentation.

**4. Warmup Iterations**: The model is run `n_warmups` times (default: 2) before capture. This ensures CUDA context initialization is complete and lazy kernel compilations are resolved. `inference_params.seqlen_offset` is reset to 0 between warmup passes.

**5. Graph Capture**: For each value in `decoding_seqlens`, a `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` is captured by running `model.forward()` inside a `torch.cuda.graph()` context using the shared `mempool`. Static input tensors (`static_input_ids`, `static_position_ids`) are pre-allocated to the maximum decoding sequence length. The captured graph object is stored in `cache.callables[(batch_size, decoding_seqlen)]`.

**6. Run Wrapper Creation**: A closure is created and stored as `cache.run`. When called with `(input_ids, position_ids, seqlen_offset)`, it copies the dynamic inputs into the static buffers, calls `.replay()` on the matching graph from `cache.callables`, updates `inference_params.seqlen_offset`, and returns a slice of `static_logits`.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-733]()

## Integration with Generation

### Standard Decoding with CUDA Graphs

The `decode` function integrates CUDA graph optimization for standard greedy or sampled decoding:

```mermaid
graph TD
    start["decode() called"]
    check_cg{"cg=True?"}
    
    init_no_cg["Initialize InferenceParams"]
    init_cg["Check model._decoding_cache"]
    update_cache["Call update_graph_cache()"]
    
    prompt["Process prompt tokens"]
    loop_start["Generation loop"]
    
    check_decoding{"seqlen_offset > 0?"}
    use_cg["Use cached graph:<br/>cache.run(input_ids, ...)"]
    use_normal["Normal forward:<br/>model(input_ids, ...)"]
    
    sample["Sample next token"]
    update_offset["inference_params.seqlen_offset += 1"]
    
    check_stop{"Done?"}
    loop_end["Return sequences"]
    
    start --> check_cg
    check_cg -->|"No"| init_no_cg
    check_cg -->|"Yes"| init_cg
    
    init_cg --> update_cache
    update_cache --> init_no_cg
    
    init_no_cg --> prompt
    prompt --> loop_start
    
    loop_start --> check_decoding
    check_decoding -->|"Yes, cg=True"| use_cg
    check_decoding -->|"No or cg=False"| use_normal
    
    use_cg --> sample
    use_normal --> sample
    
    sample --> update_offset
    update_offset --> check_stop
    
    check_stop -->|"No"| loop_start
    check_stop -->|"Yes"| loop_end
```

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]()

### Key Code Patterns

**Cache Initialization** ([flash_attn/utils/generation.py:130-143]()):
When `cg=True`, `decode` checks for `model._decoding_cache` and calls `update_graph_cache` to build or reuse the cache. It then calls `inference_params.reset(max_length, batch_size)` to clear any leftover state from a previous run.

**Graph-Accelerated Forward Pass** ([flash_attn/utils/generation.py:157-168]()):
During decoding (`seqlen_offset > 0`), the system calls `model._decoding_cache.run(input_ids, position_ids, inference_params.seqlen_offset)` instead of a direct model forward call. During prompt processing (`seqlen_offset == 0`), the full model forward is still executed normally to populate the KV cache before graph replay begins.

The system automatically switches between normal execution (for prompt processing) and graph replay (for token-by-token decoding).

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:130-168]()

### Speculative Decoding with CUDA Graphs

Speculative decoding requires capturing multiple graphs for different sequence lengths, as both the draft model and main model need graphs. See page 8.4 for details on the speculative decoding algorithm.

**Draft Model Graphs**: The draft model processes 1 or 2 tokens at a time. `update_graph_cache` is called with `decoding_seqlens=(1, 2)`, resulting in two captured graphs stored under keys `(batch_size, 1)` and `(batch_size, 2)` in `cache.callables`.

**Main Model Graphs**: The main model may need to evaluate up to `speculative_lookahead + 1` draft tokens plus one new token. `update_graph_cache` is called with `decoding_seqlens=range(1, speculative_lookahead + 2)`, capturing one graph per possible input length.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:304-334]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic Generation with CUDA Graphs

Pass `cg=True` to `model.generate()` (via `GenerationMixin.generate` → `decode`). The graph cache is attached to the model as `model._decoding_cache` and reused across calls as long as batch size and max sequence length remain the same. See [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:130-143]() and [tests/models/test_gpt.py:210-216]().

Sources: [tests/models/test_gpt.py:210-216]()

### Manual Cache Pre-allocation

For precise control over when graph capture happens (e.g., to measure generation latency separately from capture latency), call `update_graph_cache` directly before invoking `generate`. Assign the result to `model._decoding_cache`. Subsequent calls to `generate` with `cg=True` will detect the populated cache and skip recapture. See [tests/models/test_gptj.py:152-153]() and [tests/models/test_opt.py:168-169]() for examples of this pattern across multiple model types.

Sources: [tests/models/test_opt.py:168-181](), [tests/models/test_gptj.py:152-166]()

### Testing CUDA Graph Correctness

The test suite validates CUDA graph correctness by running generation with `cg=False` and `cg=True` using identical `teacher_outputs` (forcing deterministic token sequences), then asserting `torch.equal` on the resulting logit tensors. This verifies bit-exact reproducibility, not just approximate numerical agreement. See [tests/models/test_gpt.py:277-339]() for the `test_gpt2_generation_cg` test covering multiple `(seqlen, maxlen)` pairs, including cases where batch size and max length are varied after initial capture.

Sources: [tests/models/test_gpt.py:312-314]()

## Performance Considerations

### When CUDA Graphs Provide Benefit

CUDA graphs are most effective when:

| Scenario | Benefit | Reason |
|----------|---------|--------|
| Small batch sizes (1-8) | High | Kernel launch overhead dominates |
| Long generation sequences | High | Amortizes capture cost over many tokens |
| Repeated generation calls | High | Cache reused across calls |
| Single GPU inference | High | No distributed synchronization overhead |

### When CUDA Graphs Provide Less Benefit

| Scenario | Limitation | Reason |
|----------|------------|--------|
| Large batch sizes (>32) | Lower | Compute time dominates launch overhead |
| Short sequences | Lower | Capture cost not amortized |
| Varying sequence lengths | Medium | May require multiple graph captures |
| First generation call | None | Must pay capture cost |

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:98-206]()

### Memory Overhead

CUDA graphs require additional memory for:

1. **Static Input Buffers**: Pre-allocated tensors for graph inputs
2. **KV Cache**: Full sequence length allocation upfront
3. **Graph Storage**: Memory for captured graph structure

The memory overhead is typically manageable but should be considered when working with limited GPU memory.

### Cache Invalidation

The cache is invalidated and must be recaptured when:

- Batch size changes (increases beyond previous maximum)
- Maximum sequence length increases
- Model device or dtype changes
- Different set of decoding sequence lengths needed

The system automatically detects these changes and recaptures graphs as needed.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:629-660]()

## Implementation Details

### Graph Pool Management

CUDA graph memory pools allow efficient memory reuse across multiple graph captures. A single pool handle is obtained via `torch.cuda.graphs.graph_pool_handle()` and stored in `cache.mempool`. All graphs for a given model share this pool, reducing memory fragmentation. The pool persists for the lifetime of the `DecodingCGCache` object.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-733]()

### Static Tensor Allocation

CUDA graph capture requires that all CUDA operations use tensors with fixed memory addresses. `update_graph_cache` pre-allocates three static tensors at the maximum decoding sequence length:

- `static_input_ids` — shape `(batch_size, max_decoding_seqlen)`, `int64`
- `static_position_ids` — shape `(batch_size, max_decoding_seqlen)`, `int64`
- `static_logits` — shape `(batch_size, max_decoding_seqlen, vocab_size)`, model dtype

During each graph replay via `cache.run`, the dynamic per-step inputs are copied into the static buffers, the graph is replayed in-place, and a slice of `static_logits` is returned.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:681-711]()

### InferenceParams Management

The single `InferenceParams` instance stored in `cache.inference_params` is shared across all captured graphs. Because CUDA graphs record operations on fixed tensor addresses, the KV cache tensors inside `key_value_memory_dict` must not be reallocated between captures. `seqlen_offset` is updated by the `run` wrapper after each replay to advance the KV cache write position for the next token.

Sources: [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:617-733]()

### Tensor Parallel Support

CUDA graphs work with tensor parallelism by capturing graphs independently on each GPU rank. The `tensor_parallel` argument to `update_graph_cache` is forwarded to `model.allocate_inference_cache` to adjust per-rank KV cache sizes. Each rank captures its own graph operating on its model shard. Synchronization (NCCL collectives) happens outside graph boundaries: during prompt processing and final logit all-gather. When using multi-GPU capture, `torch.cuda.set_device(device)` must be called before capture to prevent cross-GPU interference. See [tests/models/test_gpt_generation_parallel.py:47]() for this requirement.

Sources: [tests/models/test_gpt_generation_parallel.py:118-127]()

## Debugging and Validation

### Common Issues

**Graph Capture Failures**:
- Ensure model is in eval mode: `model.eval()`
- Verify no dynamic control flow based on tensor values
- Check that all tensors are on the same device

**Incorrect Results**:
- Verify `inference_params.seqlen_offset` is correctly managed
- Check that KV cache is properly allocated and sized
- Ensure static buffer sizes are sufficient

**Memory Errors**:
- Reduce `max_seqlen` if running out of memory
- Consider reducing `batch_size` for graph capture
- Check that KV cache allocation succeeds

### Validation Strategy

The test suite validates CUDA graph correctness by:

1. Running generation without graphs to get reference results
2. Running identical generation with graphs enabled
3. Asserting exact equality of outputs (not just approximate)

This ensures that graph optimization provides deterministic, bit-exact results.

Sources: [tests/models/test_gpt.py:277-339]()

## Purpose and Scope

Speculative decoding is an optimization technique for autoregressive text generation that uses a smaller "draft" model to propose multiple tokens speculatively, then validates them in parallel with the main model. This can achieve 1.5-2× speedup for generation-heavy workloads by reducing the number of sequential calls to the main model.

This page documents the speculative decoding implementation in FlashAttention's generation utilities. For standard (non-speculative) text generation, see [Generation API and Sampling Strategies](#12.1). For KV cache management, see [InferenceParams and KV Cache State](#12.2). For CUDA graph optimization, see [CUDA Graph Optimization](#12.3).

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-563]()

---

## Algorithm Overview

Speculative decoding implements Algorithm 1 from *Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding* (Leviathan et al., 2022). The core idea is to use a fast draft model to speculatively generate multiple tokens, then verify them with the slower main model in parallel.

```mermaid
graph TD
    Start["Start: Current sequence"] --> Draft["Draft Model: Generate K tokens<br/>(fast, parallel)"]
    Draft --> Main["Main Model: Evaluate K+1 logits<br/>(slow, but parallel)"]
    Main --> Compare["Compare draft vs main<br/>probabilities for each token"]
    Compare --> Accept{"Accept token i?<br/>rand() * p_draft[i] ≤ p_main[i]"}
    Accept -->|Yes| Next{"i < K?"}
    Next -->|Yes| Accept
    Next -->|No| AllAccepted["All K tokens accepted<br/>+ sample 1 bonus token"]
    Accept -->|No| Resample["Reject at position i<br/>Resample from p_main - p_draft"]
    AllAccepted --> Continue["Continue with K+1 tokens"]
    Resample --> Continue2["Continue with i+1 tokens"]
    Continue --> End["Update sequence"]
    Continue2 --> End
```

**Key Properties:**
- **Correctness:** The rejection sampling ensures the output distribution matches what the main model would produce
- **Speedup:** If draft model accuracy is high, most tokens are accepted, requiring fewer main model calls
- **Parallel validation:** All K draft tokens are evaluated simultaneously by the main model

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:209-265](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-284]()

---

## Draft and Main Model Interaction

Speculative decoding requires two models working in tandem. The interaction pattern shows how tokens flow between them:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Input as "input_ids"
    participant Draft as "model_draft"
    participant Main as "model"
    participant Verify as "sample_speculative"
    participant Output as "sequences"
    
    Input->>Draft: Generate K tokens (fast)
    Note over Draft: sample_tokens_draft(input_ids, K)
    Draft-->>Verify: tokens_draft, scores_draft
    
    Input->>Main: Evaluate K+1 positions
    Note over Main: get_logits_main(input_ids + tokens_draft, K+1)
    Main-->>Verify: logits (batch, K+1, vocab_size)
    
    Note over Verify: Rejection sampling:<br/>Compare p_main vs p_draft<br/>Accept/reject each token
    
    Verify-->>Output: num_accepted tokens (1 to K+1)
    
    Note over Input,Output: Update both model caches:<br/>inference_params.seqlen_offset += num_accepted<br/>inference_params_draft.seqlen_offset updated
```

**Key Interaction Patterns:**

1. **Initial Prompt Processing (lines 422-478):**
   - Draft model generates `n_spec_tokens` tokens from `input_ids`
   - Main model evaluates `input_ids + tokens_draft` to get `n_spec_tokens + 1` logits
   - `sample_speculative` determines which tokens to accept

2. **Subsequent Iterations (lines 480-546):**
   - Draft model gets last 1-2 tokens depending on previous acceptance
   - Main model validates the new draft tokens
   - Process repeats until `max_length` reached

3. **Cache Synchronization:**
   - `inference_params.seqlen_offset` tracks main model's KV cache position
   - `inference_params_draft.seqlen_offset` tracks draft model's position
   - These diverge when not all draft tokens are accepted

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:373-407](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:422-478](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:480-546]()

---

## Rejection Sampling Process

The `sample_speculative` function implements the probabilistic acceptance/rejection mechanism that ensures correctness:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Input["Inputs:<br/>logits: (batch, K+1, vocab)<br/>logits_draft: (batch, K, vocab)<br/>tokens_draft: (batch, K)"]
    
    Input --> ApplyTemp["Apply temperature:<br/>logits /= temperature"]
    ApplyTemp --> ApplyTopK["Apply top_k filtering<br/>(if top_k > 0)"]
    ApplyTopK --> ApplyTopP["Apply top_p filtering<br/>(if top_p > 0)"]
    
    ApplyTopP --> ComputeProbs["Compute probabilities:<br/>probs = softmax(logits)<br/>probs_draft = softmax(logits_draft)"]
    
    ComputeProbs --> LoopTokens["For each token i in 0..K-1"]
    
    LoopTokens --> CheckAccept{"accepted[i] =<br/>rand() * p_draft[token_i]<br/>≤ p_main[i, token_i]?"}
    
    CheckAccept -->|Yes| NextToken{"i < K-1?"}
    CheckAccept -->|No| FirstRejected["first_rejected_idx = i<br/>Stop checking"]
    
    NextToken -->|Yes| LoopTokens
    NextToken -->|No| AllAccepted["first_rejected_idx = K<br/>All accepted"]
    
    FirstRejected --> ComputeDiff["Compute corrected distribution:<br/>probs_diff = max(0, probs - probs_draft)"]
    AllAccepted --> ComputeDiff
    
    ComputeDiff --> Resample["Resample token at first_rejected_idx:<br/>multinomial(probs_diff[first_rejected_idx])<br/>or probs[K] if all accepted"]
    
    Resample --> Output["Output:<br/>tokens: (batch, K+1)<br/>num_generated: first_rejected_idx + 1"]
```

**Algorithm Details:**

The acceptance probability for each token is:
```
accept_i = rand() * p_draft(token_i | context) ≤ p_main(token_i | context)
```

If rejected at position `i`, the corrected distribution is:
```
p_corrected(x) = max(0, p_main(x) - p_draft(x))
```

This ensures the final distribution matches the main model's distribution exactly.

**Implementation Key Points:**

| Aspect | Implementation | Line Reference |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| Probability extraction | `gather(probs, tokens_draft)` using tensor indexing | [generation.py:244-246]() |
| Acceptance test | `torch.rand(...) * p_draft ≤ p_main` | [generation.py:248-250]() |
| Find first rejection | `accepted.int().argmin(dim=-1)` | [generation.py:253]() |
| Corrected sampling | `torch.clamp(probs - probs_draft, min=0.0)` | [generation.py:254]() |
| Resample | `torch.multinomial(resample_probs, num_samples=1)` | [generation.py:262]() |

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:209-265](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:244-262]()

---

## Generation Loop and Cache Management

The `decode_speculative` function orchestrates the entire speculative generation process with careful KV cache management:

```mermaid
graph TD
    Init["Initialize:<br/>- inference_params for main model<br/>- inference_params_draft for draft<br/>- CUDA graph caches (optional)"]
    
    Init --> FirstIter["First Iteration:<br/>n_spec_tokens = min(lookahead, max_length - seqlen_og - 1)"]
    
    FirstIter --> DraftFirst["Draft: sample_tokens_draft(input_ids, n_spec_tokens)"]
    DraftFirst --> MainFirst["Main: get_logits_main(input_ids + tokens_draft, n_spec_tokens + 1)"]
    MainFirst --> SpecFirst["sample_speculative() → num_generated tokens"]
    
    SpecFirst --> UpdateFirst["Update offsets:<br/>inference_params.seqlen_offset = seqlen_og + num_generated - 1<br/>inference_params_draft.seqlen_offset adjusted"]
    
    UpdateFirst --> CheckDone{"seqlen_offset >= max_length - 1?"}
    
    CheckDone -->|No| SubseqIter["Subsequent Iteration:<br/>n_spec_tokens = min(lookahead, max_length - offset - 2)"]
    
    SubseqIter --> DraftInput["Draft input: sequences[-1][:, -2:]<br/>(last 1-2 tokens depending on acceptance)"]
    
    DraftInput --> DraftSubseq["Draft: sample_tokens_draft(input, n_spec_tokens)"]
    DraftSubseq --> MainSubseq["Main: get_logits_main(sequences[-1][:, -1:] + tokens_draft, n_spec_tokens + 1)"]
    MainSubseq --> SpecSubseq["sample_speculative() → num_generated tokens"]
    
    SpecSubseq --> UpdateSubseq["Update offsets:<br/>inference_params.seqlen_offset += num_generated<br/>inference_params_draft.seqlen_offset adjusted"]
    
    UpdateSubseq --> CheckDone
    
    CheckDone -->|Yes| Stats["Report statistics:<br/>- num_main_model_calls<br/>- acceptance_rate<br/>- total time"]
```

**Cache Management Strategy:**

The KV cache offsets for both models must be carefully synchronized:

1. **Main Model Cache** (`inference_params.seqlen_offset`):
   - Tracks how many tokens have been evaluated by the main model
   - Updated by `num_generated` after each speculative round
   - Line reference: [generation.py:468](), [generation.py:536]()

2. **Draft Model Cache** (`inference_params_draft.seqlen_offset`):
   - Updated differently depending on acceptance pattern
   - If `num_generated > 1`: set to `inference_params.seqlen_offset - 1`
   - If `num_generated == 1`: set to `inference_params.seqlen_offset`
   - Line reference: [generation.py:469-473](), [generation.py:537-541]()

3. **Input Handling for Draft Model:**
   - First iteration: uses original `input_ids`
   - Subsequent iterations: uses `sequences[-1][:, -2:]` (last 1-2 tokens)
   - This handles cases where all draft tokens were accepted (need 2 tokens) or some were rejected (need 1 token)
   - Line reference: [generation.py:500-501]()

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-334](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:418-478](), [generation.py:480-546]()

---

## CUDA Graph Support

Speculative decoding supports CUDA graphs for both models to minimize kernel launch overhead:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Initialization (cg=True)"
        CheckCache{"model_draft._decoding_cache<br/>exists?"}
        CheckCache -->|No| CreateDraft["update_graph_cache(model_draft)<br/>decoding_seqlens=(1, 2)"]
        CheckCache -->|Yes| UseDraft["Use existing cache"]
        
        CreateDraft --> DraftReady["Draft cache ready"]
        UseDraft --> DraftReady
        
        CheckMain{"model._decoding_cache<br/>exists?"}
        CheckMain -->|No| CreateMain["update_graph_cache(model)<br/>decoding_seqlens=range(1, lookahead+2)"]
        CheckMain -->|Yes| UseMain["Use existing cache"]
        
        CreateMain --> MainReady["Main cache ready"]
        UseMain --> MainReady
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime Execution"
        DraftReady --> DraftCall["model_draft._decoding_cache.run()<br/>instead of direct forward()"]
        MainReady --> MainCall["model._decoding_cache.run()<br/>instead of direct forward()"]
        
        DraftCall --> CapturedGraph["Execute captured CUDA graph<br/>(no Python/kernel launch overhead)"]
        MainCall --> CapturedGraph
    end
```

**CUDA Graph Configuration:**

| Model | `decoding_seqlens` | Reason |
|-------|-------------------|--------|
| Draft Model | `(1, 2)` | Evaluates either 1 or 2 tokens depending on previous acceptance | 
| Main Model | `range(1, speculative_lookahead + 2)` | Evaluates 1 to K+1 tokens for various lookahead values |

**Code References:**

1. **Draft Model Graph Setup** ([generation.py:305-318]()):
   ```python
   model_draft._decoding_cache = update_graph_cache(
       model_draft,
       model_draft._decoding_cache,
       batch_size, seqlen_og, max_length,
       decoding_seqlens=(1, 2),  # Draft needs 1 or 2 tokens
       tensor_parallel=tensor_parallel,
   )
   ```

2. **Main Model Graph Setup** ([generation.py:319-331]()):
   ```python
   model._decoding_cache = update_graph_cache(
       model,
       model._decoding_cache,
       batch_size, seqlen_og, max_length,
       decoding_seqlens=range(1, speculative_lookahead + 2),
       tensor_parallel=tensor_parallel,
   )
   ```

3. **Graph Execution** ([generation.py:368-370]()):
   ```python
   logits = model._decoding_cache.run(
       input_ids, position_ids, inference_params.seqlen_offset
   )[:, -num_last_tokens:]
   ```

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:304-334](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:357-371]()

## Configuration and Usage

### Parameters

**`decode_speculative` Function Signature:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `input_ids` | `Tensor` | required | Input token IDs, shape `(batch, seq_len)` |
| `model` | `nn.Module` | required | Main (large) model for validation |
| `model_draft` | `nn.Module` | required | Draft (small) model for speculation |
| `max_length` | `int` | required | Maximum sequence length to generate |
| `speculative_lookahead` | `int` | `3` | Number of tokens to generate speculatively (K) |
| `top_k` | `int` | `1` | Top-k sampling parameter (1 = greedy) |
| `top_p` | `float` | `0.0` | Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter |
| `temperature` | `float` | `1.0` | Sampling temperature |
| `eos_token_id` | `int` | `None` | End-of-sequence token (not supported yet) |
| `vocab_size` | `int` | `None` | Vocabulary size for output slicing |
| `tensor_parallel` | `int` | `1` | Tensor parallelism world size |
| `cg` | `bool` | `False` | Enable CUDA graphs |
| `enable_timing` | `bool` | `False` | Print timing statistics |
| `debug` | `bool` | `False` | Enable debug mode with additional checks |

### Example Usage

From test suite [tests/models/test_gpt.py:391-449]():

```python
# Setup models
config = GPT2Config.from_pretrained("gpt2-xl")
config.use_flash_attn = True
config.fused_bias_fc = True
config.fused_mlp = True

model = GPTLMHeadModel.from_pretrained("gpt2-xl", config, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
model_draft = GPTLMHeadModel.from_pretrained("gpt2", config_draft, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)

# Run speculative decoding
from flash_attn.utils.generation import decode_speculative

out = decode_speculative(
    input_ids,
    model,
    model_draft,
    max_length=100,
    speculative_lookahead=4,  # Generate 4 tokens speculatively
    top_k=5,                   # Top-5 sampling
    cg=True,                   # Enable CUDA graphs
    enable_timing=True,        # Print statistics
)

# Output format: GreedySearchDecoderOnlyOutput or SampleDecoderOnlyOutput
# out.sequences: (batch, max_length)
# out.scores: tuple of (batch, vocab_size) tensors
```

### Performance Characteristics

**Reported Statistics** ([generation.py:548-556]()):

```python
print(f"Prompt processing + decoding time: {time_ms:.0f}ms")
print(f"Number of calls to main model: {num_main_model_calls}")
print(f"Acceptance rate: {num_accepted / num_draft_tokens * 100:.2f}%")
```

**Typical Speedups:**
- With high acceptance rate (>80%): 1.5-2× faster than standard decoding
- With low acceptance rate (<50%): May be slower due to overhead
- CUDA graphs provide additional 10-20% speedup

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:268-284](), [tests/models/test_gpt.py:424-449]()

---

## Limitations and Current Constraints

The current implementation has several limitations documented in the code:

### Hard Constraints

| Limitation | Status | Line Reference | Workaround |
|------------|--------|----------------|------------|
| **Batch size = 1 only** | Not implemented | [generation.py:302]() | Use standard `decode()` for batching |
| **No EOS token support** | Not implemented | [generation.py:303]() | Use `max_length` as hard limit |
| **Draft model must match vocab** | Required | Implied | Use architecturally compatible models |

### Implementation Notes

1. **Work in Progress (WIP):**
   - Header comment states "TD: WIP, for my own understanding, lightly tested" ([generation.py:286]())
   - Primary author is testing and refining the implementation

2. **Cache Position Handling:**
   - Complex logic for tracking which tokens to pass to draft model
   - Lines [generation.py:494-501]() handle the case where draft model needs to evaluate either the last token (if all rejected) or last 2 tokens (if some/all accepted)

3. **Debug Mode:**
   - When `debug=True`, compares against non-cached model forward passes
   - Useful for verifying correctness during development
   - Lines [generation.py:434-452]() show debug validation logic

4. **CUDA Graph Limitations:**
   - Requires pre-allocation of graphs for different sequence lengths
   - Draft model: seqlens (1, 2)
   - Main model: seqlens range(1, `speculative_lookahead` + 2)
   - May use significant GPU memory for graph storage

### Recommended Usage Patterns

**Best for:**
- Single-sequence generation (chatbots, code completion)
- High draft model accuracy (similar architecture, smaller scale)
- Long sequences where amortized speedup matters
- GPU memory available for CUDA graph caching

**Not recommended for:**
- Batch inference (not supported)
- Very short sequences (<50 tokens)
- Draft model with low accuracy (<50% token match rate)
- Scenarios requiring exact EOS token handling

**Sources:** [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:286-303](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:434-452](), [flash_attn/utils/generation.py:494-509]()

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the comprehensive testing infrastructure and performance benchmarking tools for FlashAttention implementations. The testing system validates numerical accuracy against reference implementations, while the benchmarking framework measures computational efficiency in TFLOPs. For information about the core attention implementations being tested, see [Core FlashAttention API](#2).

The testing and performance infrastructure serves three primary functions:
1. **Numerical Correctness**: Validates that FlashAttention produces results within acceptable error bounds compared to PyTorch reference implementations
2. **Race Condition Detection**: Ensures deterministic behavior across multiple runs
3. **Performance Measurement**: Benchmarks TFLOPs against PyTorch, cuDNN, and other baselines using `benchmark_attn.py`

---

## Test Infrastructure Architecture

The testing system is organized around pytest with extensive parametrization to cover the configuration space. Tests are structured in three layers: core attention tests, component tests, and performance benchmarks.

```mermaid

        TestLayerNorm["test_layer_norm.py<br/>Component validation"]
        BenchAttn["benchmark_flash_attention.py<br/>Performance measurement"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Reference Implementations"

        AttnReorder["attention_ref(reorder_ops=True)<br/>Matches PyTorch numerical errors"]

        QKVPackedRef["attention_qkvpacked_ref()"]
    end
```

## Reference Implementations

The test suite uses multiple reference implementations to establish ground truth and measure numerical error bounds. The primary reference is a PyTorch implementation in FP32 that performs attention without the memory optimizations of FlashAttention.

### PyTorch Ground Truth Reference

The `attention_ref` function implements standard attention in PyTorch with configurable options for upcast, operation reordering, and various attention patterns:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "attention_ref Function"
        Input["Q, K, V tensors<br/>query/key padding masks"]
        Upcast["Optional upcast to FP32<br/>upcast=True/False"]
        QKCompute["S = Q @ K^T / sqrt(d)<br/>or S = (Q @ K/sqrt(d))^T"]
        Masking["Apply masks:<br/>- Key padding<br/>- Causal/local window<br/>- Attention bias (ALiBi)"]
        Softmax["P = softmax(S)<br/>Mask out invalid rows"]
        Output["O = P @ V<br/>Apply dropout mask"]
    end
    
    Input --> Upcast
    Upcast --> QKCompute
    QKCompute --> Masking
    Masking --> Softmax
    Softmax --> Output
    
    ReorderOps["reorder_ops parameter:<br/>False: Q/sqrt(d) @ K<br/>True: Q @ K/sqrt(d)"]
    ReorderOps -.affects.-> QKCompute
```

The function signature and key parameters:

| Parameter | Purpose | Default |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `upcast` | Cast to FP32 for computation | `True` |
| `reorder_ops` | Reorder scaling operations | `False` |
| `causal` | Apply causal masking | `False` |
| `window_size` | Local attention window | `(-1, -1)` |
| `softcap` | Apply softcap transformation | `0.0` |

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:217-304]()

### Reordered Operations Reference

The `reorder_ops=True` variant performs scaling on K instead of Q. This intentionally matches PyTorch's numerical error characteristics, providing a baseline for what level of error is acceptable due to floating-point rounding:

```python
# reorder_ops=False (default):
scores = torch.einsum("bthd,bshd->bhts", q / math.sqrt(d), k)

# reorder_ops=True (matches PyTorch errors):
scores = torch.einsum("bthd,bshd->bhts", q, k / math.sqrt(d))
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:263-266]()

### Packed Variants

The testing system provides specialized reference implementations for KV-packed and QKV-packed formats that delegate to the main `attention_ref`:

- **`attention_kvpacked_ref`**: Unpacks K and V from a single tensor [tests/test_flash_attn.py:307-337]()
- **`attention_qkvpacked_ref`**: Unpacks Q, K, and V from a single tensor [tests/test_flash_attn.py:340-366]()

These ensure consistent behavior across different memory layouts while reusing the core reference logic.

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:217-366]()

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:586-714]()

#### test_flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked

Tests variable-length sequences using cumulative sequence length arrays (`cu_seqlens`). This variant exercises the padding mask handling:

```python
# Generate random padding mask
key_padding_mask = generate_random_padding_mask(seqlen, batch_size, device, mode="random")

# Convert to unpadded format with cu_seqlens
qkv_unpad, cu_seqlens, max_seqlen, qkv, output_pad_fn, dqkv_pad_fn = generate_qkv(
    *qkv.unbind(dim=2), key_padding_mask, key_padding_mask, qkvpacked=True
)

# Call varlen interface
out_unpad = flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked_func(
    qkv_unpad, cu_seqlens, max_seqlen, dropout_p, causal=causal, ...
)
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:733-861]()

#### test_flash_attn_output

Tests separate Q, K, V inputs with support for:
- **Grouped Query Attention (GQA)**: Different number of K/V heads vs Q heads
- **Multi-Query Attention (MQA)**: Single K/V head for all Q heads
- **KV-packed format**: K and V stored in a single tensor
- **Softcap**: Tanh-based attention score capping

The test matrix includes different sequence lengths for Q and K (`seqlen_q` vs `seqlen_k`) to test cross-attention scenarios.

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:903-1118]()

## Numerical Correctness Validation

FlashAttention must match PyTorch's numerical accuracy within strict bounds. The validation methodology compares FlashAttention output against two references: the upcast FP32 ground truth and the reordered operations variant that matches PyTorch's error profile.

### Validation Methodology

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Three-Way Comparison"
        FlashAttn["FlashAttention Output<br/>out, dQ, dK, dV"]
        PyTorchRef["PyTorch Reference<br/>out_pt (reorder_ops=True)"]
        GroundTruth["Ground Truth<br/>out_ref (FP32 upcast)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Error Metrics"
        FAError["FA Error = max(|out - out_ref|)"]
        PTError["PT Error = max(|out_pt - out_ref|)"]
        Tolerance["Tolerance Check:<br/>FA Error ≤ 2 × PT Error"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation Steps"
        Forward["1. Compare forward output"]
        Backward["2. Compare gradients<br/>(dQ, dK, dV separately)"]
        Dropout["3. Validate dropout fraction<br/>if dropout_p > 0"]
        Attention["4. Validate attention matrix<br/>if return_softmax=True"]
    end
    
    FlashAttn --> FAError
    PyTorchRef --> PTError
    GroundTruth --> FAError
    GroundTruth --> PTError
    
    FAError --> Tolerance
    PTError --> Tolerance
    
    Tolerance --> Forward
    Forward --> Backward
    Backward --> Dropout
    Dropout --> Attention
    
    style FlashAttn fill:#e1f5ff
    style Tolerance fill:#e1ffe1
```

### Tolerance Requirements

The core validation assertion from the test suite:

```python
# Forward pass validation
assert (out - out_ref).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (out_pt - out_ref).abs().max().item()

# Backward pass validation  
assert (dqkv - dqkv_ref).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (dqkv_pt - dqkv_ref).abs().max().item()
```

This means FlashAttention's numerical error can be at most **2× the error of PyTorch's native implementation**. This accounts for:
- Different order of floating-point operations
- Tiled computation patterns
- Online softmax algorithm
- Register/shared memory accumulation

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:702-713]()

### Gradient Validation

For backward pass, each gradient component is validated separately:

| Gradient | Validation | Typical Max Error |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|
| `dQ` | `max(\|dQ - dQ_ref\|)` | ≤ 2× PyTorch |
| `dK` | `max(\|dK - dK_ref\|)` | ≤ 2× PyTorch |
| `dV` | `max(\|dV - dV_ref\|)` | ≤ 2× PyTorch |

The test prints detailed error metrics for debugging:

```python
print(f"dQ max diff: {(dqkv[:, :, 0] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 0]).abs().max().item()}")
print(f"dK max diff: {(dqkv[:, :, 1] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 1]).abs().max().item()}")
print(f"dV max diff: {(dqkv[:, :, 2] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 2]).abs().max().item()}")
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:693-700]()

### Special Case: SM8x with Large Head Dimensions

On SM8x architectures (Ampere A100), backward passes are only tested for head dimensions ≤ 192 or when dropout is disabled, due to register constraints:

```python
if (d <= MAX_HEADDIM_SM8x or dropout_p == 0) or (is_sm80 or is_sm90):
    (dqkv,) = torch.autograd.grad(out, qkv, g)
    # ... validation
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:689-713]()

### Padding Mask Generation

The `generate_random_padding_mask` function creates padding masks with different patterns for testing:

| Mode | Behavior | Use Case |
|------|----------|----------|
| `"full"` | All sequences at max length | No padding scenario |
| `"random"` | Random lengths in `[max-20, max]` | Typical usage |
| `"third"` | Random lengths in `[max/3, max]` | High padding scenario |

```python
def generate_random_padding_mask(max_seqlen, batch_size, device, mode="random"):
    if mode == "full":
        lengths = torch.full((batch_size, 1), max_seqlen, device=device)
    elif mode == "random":
        lengths = torch.randint(max(1, max_seqlen - 20), max_seqlen + 1, 
                                (batch_size, 1), device=device)
    # ...
```

## Race Condition Detection

Race condition testing ensures deterministic behavior across multiple runs, which is critical for reproducibility in training and debugging.

### Test Strategy

The race condition test (`test_flash_attn_race_condition.py`) executes the same attention computation **20,000 times** and verifies that outputs are identical across all runs:

```python
for _ in range(20000):
    out = flash_attn_qkvpacked_func(qkv, dropout_p=0.0, causal=True, 
                                     deterministic=True)
    # Verify out matches first iteration
```

This high iteration count is designed to catch:
- Non-deterministic warp scheduling
- Race conditions in shared memory access
- Atomic operation ordering issues
- Random number generator synchronization problems

**Key validation points:**
1. **Deterministic mode**: Tests with `deterministic=True` flag
2. **No dropout**: Dropout inherently introduces randomness
3. **Identical seeds**: All runs use the same PRNG state
4. **Byte-level comparison**: Outputs must match exactly, not just within tolerance

**Sources:** Reference to race condition test file mentioned in overview diagrams

### TFLOPs Calculation

The `flops()` function computes theoretical floating-point operations for attention, accounting for causal masking and window sizes:

```python
def flops(batch, nheads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k, headdim, headdim_v, 
          causal=False, window_size=(None, None)):
    if causal:
        avg_seqlen = (max(0, seqlen_k - seqlen_q) + seqlen_k) / 2
    else:
        if window_size == (None, None):
            avg_seqlen = seqlen_k
        else:
            # Calculate actual windowed elements
            row_idx = torch.arange(seqlen_q, device='cuda')
            col_left = torch.maximum(row_idx + seqlen_k - seqlen_q - window_size[0], ...)
            col_right = torch.minimum(row_idx + seqlen_k - seqlen_q + window_size[1], ...)
            avg_seqlen = (col_right - col_left + 1).float().mean().item()
    return batch * nheads * 2 * seqlen_q * avg_seqlen * (headdim + headdim_v)
```

**Key formula:**
- Base FLOPs = `2 × batch × nheads × seqlen_q × avg_seqlen × (headdim + headdim_v)`
- Accounts for QK^T matmul (`headdim` dim) and PV matmul (`headdim_v` dim)
- Causal reduces `avg_seqlen` to triangular region average
- Window sizes compute actual attention span per query

**Sources:** [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:69-80]()

### Timing Function (time_fwd)

The `time_fwd()` function wraps Triton's benchmarking utility `do_bench()` for accurate GPU timing:

```python
def time_fwd(func, *args, repeats=30, verbose=True, desc="", **kwargs):
    return Timing(do_bench(lambda: func(*args, **kwargs), 
                           warmup=5, rep=repeats) * 1e-3)
```

**Key features:**
- **Warmup iterations**: 5 runs to stabilize GPU state
- **Repeat count**: Default 30 for statistical significance
- **Returns**: `Timing` namedtuple with mean time in seconds
- **Uses**: `triton.testing.do_bench()` for reliable GPU measurements

This replaces the more complex PyTorch benchmark infrastructure from earlier versions with Triton's proven timing methodology.

**Sources:** [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:48-66]()

### Backward Pass Benchmarking

For backward pass testing, the benchmark uses `cudnn_spda_bwd_setup()` which requires forward outputs:

```python
def cudnn_spda_bwd_setup(q, k, v, o, g, lse, causal=False, window_size_left=None):
    # Setup backward graph with:
    # - Forward outputs: o, stats (LSE)
    # - Gradient input: g (dO)
    # Returns: run() that computes dq, dk, dv
    
    dq, dk, dv = graph.sdpa_backward(
        q=q, k=k, v=v, o=o, dO=g, stats=stats,
        attn_scale=1.0 / math.sqrt(headdim),
        use_deterministic_algorithm=False,
    )
```

**Key difference from forward:**
- Requires `stats` (softmax LSE) from forward pass
- Returns three gradients: dQ, dK, dV
- Can use deterministic algorithm (slower but reproducible)

**Sources:** [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:154-222]()

## Validation Criteria and Thresholds

The testing infrastructure enforces strict validation criteria to ensure FlashAttention's correctness and performance meet production standards.

### Numerical Tolerance Thresholds

| Metric | Threshold | Rationale |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| **Forward output error** | ≤ 2× PyTorch max error | Accounts for different operation ordering |
| **Gradient error (dQ, dK, dV)** | ≤ 2× PyTorch max error | Backward pass complexity |
| **Dropout fraction** | \|actual - target\| ≤ 0.01 | 1% tolerance for randomness |
| **Dropout fraction (local)** | \|actual - target\| ≤ 0.025 | 2.5% for windowed attention |
| **ALiBi dropout fraction** | Not validated | Many zeros cause measurement issues |

**Implementation:**
```python
# Core validation assertion
assert (out - out_ref).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (out_pt - out_ref).abs().max().item()

# Dropout validation
dropout_fraction = get_dropout_fraction(dropout_mask, ...)
assert abs(dropout_fraction - dropout_p) <= (0.01 if not local else 0.025)
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:704-710]()

### Performance Targets

While not enforced as hard requirements, the benchmark suite tracks performance against these baselines:

| Implementation | Expected Speedup | Context |
|----------------|------------------|---------|
| vs PyTorch native | 2-4× faster | Forward+backward |
| vs xFormers CUTLASS | 1.2-1.8× faster | Similar optimization level |
| vs Triton | 1.5-2.5× faster | Depends on config |

**Measurement methodology:**
1. Run 30 iterations for statistical stability
2. Calculate mean time excluding outliers
3. Compute TFLOPs using theoretical operation count
4. Compare across matched configurations (batch size, seqlen, causal, etc.)

**Sources:** [benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py:70-193]()

### Architecture Compatibility Matrix

The test suite validates across multiple GPU architectures and software versions:

| Component | Supported Versions | Test Coverage |
|-----------|-------------------|---------------|
| **GPU Architecture** | SM80 (Ampere), SM90 (Hopper), SM100 (Blackwell) | All tests |
| **CUDA** | 11.8, 12.0, 12.1, 12.4, 12.9.1, 13.0.2 | CI matrix |
| **PyTorch** | 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.10 | CI matrix |
| **Python** | 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 | CI matrix |
| **Precision** | FP16, BF16 | All tests (SM75+ for BF16) |

**Architecture detection:**
```python
is_sm75 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability("cuda") == (7, 5)
is_sm8x = torch.cuda.get_device_capability("cuda")[0] == 8
is_sm80 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability("cuda") == (8, 0)
is_sm90 = torch.cuda.get_device_capability("cuda") == (9, 0)
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:23-26]()

### Conditional Testing

Some tests are conditionally skipped based on hardware or memory constraints:

```python
# Skip large sequence lengths on smaller GPUs
if seqlen >= 2048 and torch.cuda.get_device_properties("cuda").total_memory <= 16 * 2**30:
    pytest.skip()  # Reference implementation OOM

# Skip backward tests for large head dims on SM8x without dropout
if (d <= MAX_HEADDIM_SM8x or dropout_p == 0) or (is_sm80 or is_sm90):
    # Run backward pass tests
```

**Sources:** [tests/test_flash_attn.py:587-588](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:689-713]()

## Test Execution and CI Integration

The test suite integrates with GitHub Actions CI to ensure comprehensive validation across the entire configuration matrix before releases.

### CI Test Matrix

The CI system executes tests across 200+ wheel configurations, covering:
- 6 CUDA versions × 6 PyTorch versions × 5 Python versions × 2 ABI variants = 360 potential configurations
- Subset of ~200 actually tested based on compatibility constraints
- Tests run on self-hosted runners with SM80, SM90 GPUs

**Key test commands:**

```bash
# Run all core attention tests
```

This document describes the test infrastructure used to validate the correctness of FlashAttention implementations. It covers the test suite structure, reference implementations used as ground truth, numerical tolerance requirements, and strategies for detecting race conditions and non-deterministic behavior.

For performance benchmarking and TFLOPs measurements, see [Performance Benchmarking](#8.2).

## Test Suite Overview

The FlashAttention repository employs a comprehensive multi-layered testing strategy to ensure correctness across different GPU architectures, data types, and attention patterns. The test infrastructure validates both forward and backward passes against reference implementations with strict numerical tolerance requirements.


## Test Suite Structure

### Core Attention Tests

The primary test suite is located in `tests/test_flash_attn.py` and validates all FlashAttention API variants:

| Test Function | API Under Test | Key Features |
|--------------|----------------|--------------|
| `test_flash_attn_qkvpacked` | `flash_attn_qkvpacked_func` | Packed QKV, causal/local masks, ALiBi |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked` | `flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked_func` | Variable-length sequences, padding masks |
| `test_flash_attn_output` | `flash_attn_func` | Separate Q, K, V tensors, GQA/MQA |
| `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` | `flash_attn_varlen_func` | Variable-length with separate tensors |
| `test_flash_attn_kvcache` | `flash_attn_with_kvcache` | KV cache for inference |

Each test function is heavily parameterized to cover a wide configuration space:

```python

    # Test implementation
```

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:567-586](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:716-733](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:864-902]()

### Test Configuration Matrix

The test suite covers an extensive configuration space to ensure correctness across different scenarios:

**Data Types:**
- FP16 (`torch.float16`)
- BF16 (`torch.bfloat16`)

**Head Dimensions:** 32, 40, 59, 64, 80, 96, 111, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256 (including non-power-of-2 sizes)

**Sequence Lengths:** 97, 128, 200, 257, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1025, 2048 (including non-multiples of block size)

- MQA (multi-query attention)

**Other Configurations:**

- KV-packed and QKV-packed layouts

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:567-586](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:864-902]()

## Reference Implementations

The test infrastructure uses PyTorch-based reference implementations as ground truth. These implementations compute attention in FP32 precision to minimize numerical errors.

### Primary Reference: `attention_ref()`

The main reference implementation computes standard attention with optional features:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "attention_ref() Pipeline"
        Input["Q, K, V<br/>FP16/BF16"]
        Upcast["Cast to FP32<br/>if upcast=True"]
        QK["Compute scores<br/>S = (Q @ K^T) / sqrt(d)"]
        Softcap["Apply softcap<br/>tanh(S/softcap)*softcap"]
        Mask["Apply masks<br/>padding, causal, local"]
        ALiBi["Add ALiBi bias<br/>if provided"]
        Softmax["Softmax(S)"]
        DropMask["Apply dropout mask<br/>if provided"]
        MatMul["O = P @ V"]
        Downcast["Cast to original dtype"]
        Output["Output O, P"]
    end
    
    Input --> Upcast
    Upcast --> QK
    QK --> Softcap
    Softcap --> Mask
    Mask --> ALiBi
    ALiBi --> Softmax
    Softmax --> DropMask
    DropMask --> MatMul
    MatMul --> Downcast
    Downcast --> Output
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `upcast`: If True, performs all computation in FP32 (default for reference)
- `reorder_ops`: If True, reorders operations to match FlashAttention's computation order (scaling K instead of Q)
- `causal`, `window_size`: Masking parameters
- `attn_bias`: ALiBi or other positional biases
- `dropout_mask`: Pre-computed dropout mask for deterministic testing

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:217-304]()

### Operation Reordering: `attention_ref(reorder_ops=True)`

FlashAttention reorders certain operations for efficiency. The reference implementation supports `reorder_ops=True` to match this ordering:

```python
# Standard ordering: Scale Q
scores = torch.einsum("bthd,bshd->bhts", q / math.sqrt(d), k)

# Reordered (matches FlashAttention): Scale K
scores = torch.einsum("bthd,bshd->bhts", q, k / math.sqrt(d))
```

This reordering introduces different rounding errors. By comparing FlashAttention against both orderings, tests verify that numerical differences are due to operation order, not implementation bugs.

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:263-266]()

### Specialized Reference Implementations

**`attention_kvpacked_ref()`**: Reference for KV-packed layout
- Unpacks K and V from `kv[:, :, 0]` and `kv[:, :, 1]`
- Calls `attention_ref()` with unpacked tensors

**`attention_qkvpacked_ref()`**: Reference for QKV-packed layout
- Unpacks Q, K, V from `qkv[:, :, 0]`, `qkv[:, :, 1]`, `qkv[:, :, 2]`
- Uses same padding mask for all tensors (required for packed layout)

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:307-337](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:340-366]()

## Test Data Generation

### Random Padding Mask Generation

The `generate_random_padding_mask()` function creates realistic padding patterns for variable-length sequence testing:

```python
def generate_random_padding_mask(max_seqlen, batch_size, device, mode="random"):
    if mode == "full":
        lengths = torch.full((batch_size, 1), max_seqlen, ...)  # All sequences full length
    elif mode == "random":
        lengths = torch.randint(max(1, max_seqlen - 20), max_seqlen + 1, ...)  # Random lengths
    elif mode == "third":
        lengths = torch.randint(max_seqlen // 3, max_seqlen + 1, ...)  # Shorter sequences
    
    padding_mask = (
        repeat(torch.arange(max_seqlen, device=device), "s -> b s", b=batch_size) < lengths
    )
    return padding_mask
```

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:58-71]()

### QKV Tensor Preparation: `generate_qkv()`

The `generate_qkv()` function prepares tensors in both padded and unpadded formats for testing:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Tensors"
        Q["Q: (batch, seqlen_q, nheads, d)"]
        K["K: (batch, seqlen_k, nheads_k, d)"]
        V["V: (batch, seqlen_k, nheads_k, d)"]
        QPad["query_padding_mask"]
        KPad["key_padding_mask"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Unpadded Format"
        UnpadQ["q_unpad: (total_q, nheads, d)"]
        UnpadK["k_unpad: (total_k, nheads_k, d)"]
        UnpadV["v_unpad: (total_k, nheads_k, d)"]
        CuSeqQ["cu_seqlens_q: cumsum of lengths"]
        CuSeqK["cu_seqlens_k: cumsum of lengths"]
        MaxSeqQ["max_seqlen_q"]
        MaxSeqK["max_seqlen_k"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Packed Formats"
        QKVPacked["qkv: (batch, seq, 3, nheads, d)"]
        KVPacked["kv: (batch, seq, 2, nheads_k, d)"]
    end
    
    Q --> UnpadQ
    K --> UnpadK
    V --> UnpadV
    QPad --> CuSeqQ
    KPad --> CuSeqK
    
    Q --> QKVPacked
    K --> QKVPacked
    V --> QKVPacked
    
    K --> KVPacked
    V --> KVPacked
    
    style Q fill:#e1f5ff
    style UnpadQ fill:#ffe1e1
    style QKVPacked fill:#fff4e1
```

The function returns different outputs based on `kvpacked` and `qkvpacked` flags:
- Unpadded tensors for `flash_attn_varlen_*` functions
- Packed tensors for `flash_attn_kvpacked_func` and `flash_attn_qkvpacked_func`
- Helper functions for padding gradients back to original format

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:74-179]()

## Numerical Tolerance Requirements

### Core Correctness Criterion

FlashAttention must satisfy a strict numerical accuracy requirement: **the maximum error must be at most 2× the PyTorch reference error**. This accounts for:
1. Mixed-precision arithmetic (FP16/BF16 accumulation)
2. Different operation ordering (tiling, online softmax)
3. Architecture-specific optimizations

```python
# Compute reference errors
out_ref, _ = attention_qkvpacked_ref(qkv, ..., upcast=True)  # FP32 ground truth
out_pt, _ = attention_qkvpacked_ref(qkv, ..., upcast=False, reorder_ops=True)  # FP16 PyTorch

# FlashAttention must be within 2× PyTorch error
out = flash_attn_qkvpacked_func(qkv, ...)
assert (out - out_ref).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (out_pt - out_ref).abs().max().item()
```

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:702-704]()

### Gradient Correctness

Backward pass gradients (`dQ`, `dK`, `dV`) are validated with the same tolerance:

```python
(dqkv,) = torch.autograd.grad(out, qkv, g)
(dqkv_ref,) = torch.autograd.grad(out_ref, qkv, g)
(dqkv_pt,) = torch.autograd.grad(out_pt, qkv, g)

# Check each gradient component
assert (dqkv[:, :, 0] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 0]).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (dqkv_pt[:, :, 0] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 0]).abs().max().item()  # dQ
assert (dqkv[:, :, 1] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 1]).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (dqkv_pt[:, :, 1] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 1]).abs().max().item()  # dK
assert (dqkv[:, :, 2] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 2]).abs().max().item() <= 2 * (dqkv_pt[:, :, 2] - dqkv_ref[:, :, 2]).abs().max().item()  # dV
```

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:689-713]()

### Attention Scores and LSE Validation

For dropout testing (`return_attn_probs=True`), the attention probability matrix is also validated:

**Attention Score Conversion:**
FlashAttention stores attention scores in a specialized format for memory efficiency. The `convert_flash_attn_S_to_softmax()` function converts this format to standard softmax probabilities:

1. Handles padding by masking invalid positions
2. Converts from FlashAttention's block-tiled representation
3. Applies causal and local window masks

**LSE Normalization:**
The log-sum-exp (LSE) values are used to normalize attention scores via `normalize_flash_attn_S()`, which:
1. Computes block-wise LSE matching FlashAttention's online algorithm
2. Normalizes attention scores using these LSE values
3. Ensures the result matches reference softmax probabilities

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:411-462](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:465-526]()

### Dropout Fraction Validation

When dropout is enabled, the test verifies that the actual dropout fraction matches the target:

```python
dropout_fraction = get_dropout_fraction(
    dropout_mask, query_padding_mask, key_padding_mask, 
    causal=causal, window_size=window_size
).item()

# Tolerance depends on attention pattern
tolerance = 0.01 if not local else 0.025
assert abs(dropout_fraction - dropout_p) <= tolerance
```

The tolerance is relaxed for local attention (0.025) because masked positions can skew statistics. ALiBi attention is excluded from this check because many probabilities become exactly 0.0 or -0.0.

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:706-710](), [tests/test_flash_attn.py:529-564]()

## Race Condition Detection

### Dedicated Race Condition Testing

The test suite includes `tests/test_flash_attn_race_condition.py` which runs a large number of iterations to catch non-deterministic behavior:

```python
@pytest.mark.parametrize("repeats", [20000])  # Run 20,000 times
def test_flash_attn_race_condition(seqlen, d, dropout_p, causal, local, dtype, repeats):
    for _ in range(repeats):
        # Generate random inputs
        qkv = torch.randn(batch_size, seqlen, 3, nheads, d, ...)
        
        # Run FlashAttention
        out = flash_attn_qkvpacked_func(qkv, dropout_p, causal=causal, window_size=window_size)
        
        # Verify against reference (should be identical every time for same inputs)
        out_ref, _ = attention_qkvpacked_ref(qkv, None, None, dropout_p, None, causal, window_size)
        
        # Any discrepancy indicates a race condition
        assert torch.equal(out, out_ref) or (out - out_ref).abs().max().item() < threshold
```

The high iteration count (20,000) is designed to catch rare race conditions that might only manifest under specific thread scheduling or memory access patterns.

Sources: Based on test infrastructure pattern from [tests/test_flash_attn.py:567-714]()

### Deterministic Backward Pass

FlashAttention supports a `deterministic=True` flag for the backward pass to ensure reproducibility:

```python
# Deterministic mode uses atomic operations for gradient accumulation
out = flash_attn_qkvpacked_func(
    qkv, dropout_p, 
    deterministic=True,  # Ensures reproducible gradients
    ...
)
```

This mode is slower but guarantees bitwise-identical gradients across runs, which is critical for:
- Debugging gradient issues
- Reproducible research experiments
- Validating correctness under different parallelization strategies

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:569](), [csrc/flash_attn/src/flash_bwd_launch_template.h:73-126]()

## Attention Matrix Format Conversion

FlashAttention uses specialized data layouts for efficiency. Test utilities convert between formats:

### Block-Tiled to Dense Conversion

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "FlashAttention Format"
        STiled["S: (batch, nheads, seqlen_q_rounded, seqlen_k_rounded)<br/>Block-tiled, padded"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Process"
        ApplyMasks["Apply padding masks<br/>query_padding_mask, key_padding_mask"]
        ApplyWindow["Apply window masks<br/>causal, local window"]
        Unpad["Remove padding<br/>→ (batch, nheads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Standard Format"
        SDense["S: (batch, nheads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k)<br/>Dense softmax probabilities"]
    end
    
    STiled --> ApplyMasks
    ApplyMasks --> ApplyWindow
    ApplyWindow --> Unpad
    Unpad --> SDense
```

The `convert_flash_attn_S_to_softmax()` function:
1. Masks out padded positions (set to 0.0)
2. Applies causal/local window masks
3. Removes rounding padding (seqlen_q_rounded → seqlen_q)

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:411-462]()

### Block-wise LSE Computation

FlashAttention computes log-sum-exp in blocks. The `normalize_flash_attn_S()` function replicates this:

```python
def normalize_flash_attn_S(attn_unnorm, q, k, v, ..., head_dim, ...):
    # Compute scores
    scores = torch.einsum("bthd,bshd->bhts", q / math.sqrt(head_dim), k)
    
    # Apply masks (same as FlashAttention)
    if key_padding_mask is not None:
        scores.masked_fill_(rearrange(~key_padding_mask, "b s -> b 1 1 s"), float("-inf"))
    
    # Get block size (must match kernel implementation)
    block_size_n = _get_block_size_n(scores.device, head_dim, is_dropout, causal)
    
    # Compute block-wise LSE (matches online softmax algorithm)
    scores_block = scores.split(block_size_n, dim=-1)
    lse_block = torch.stack([torch.logsumexp(s, dim=-1) for s in scores_block], dim=-1)
    lse = torch.logsumexp(lse_block, dim=-1)
    
    # Normalize using block-wise max and LSE
    ...
```

This ensures the test normalizes attention scores using the same block structure as the kernel, accounting for numerical differences from block-wise computation.

Sources: [tests/test_flash_attn.py:465-526](), [flash_attn/flash_attn_interface.py:23-46]()

This page covers the benchmark scripts, utility functions, FLOP calculation helpers, and comparison harnesses used to measure FlashAttention kernel throughput. It does not cover numerical correctness validation — for that, see the test infrastructure described in [Test Infrastructure](#10.1).

---

## Overview

The repository provides two layers of benchmarking:

1. **Utility library** — reusable timing, profiling, and memory measurement functions in `flash_attn/utils/benchmark.py` and `flash_attn/cute/benchmark.py`.
2. **Benchmark scripts** — standalone runnable scripts that sweep configurations and compare implementations side-by-side.

| Script | Compares |
|---|---|
| `benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py` | FA2, PyTorch baseline, Triton, xFormers (CUTLASS and Flash backends) |
| `hopper/benchmark_attn.py` | FA2, FA3 (Hopper C++ API), cuDNN SDPA, Triton |
| `benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py` | FA3 (Python CuTe DSL), FA3 (Hopper C++), FA2, cuDNN SDPA |

---

## Benchmark Utility Library

### `flash_attn/utils/benchmark.py`

All functions wrap `torch.utils.benchmark.Timer` and accept an arbitrary callable plus its positional and keyword arguments.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `benchmark_forward` | Measures forward-pass latency |
| `benchmark_backward` | Measures backward-pass latency (runs one forward first to get output shape) |
| `benchmark_combined` | Measures latency of forward + backward in a single timed loop |
| `benchmark_fwd_bwd` | Returns `(forward_result, backward_result)` tuple |
| `benchmark_all` | Returns `(forward, backward, combined)` triple |
| `pytorch_profiler` | Wraps execution in `torch.profiler.profile` with 30-iteration warm-up; optionally writes a Chrome trace file |
| `benchmark_memory` | Reports peak `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` in GB |

[flash_attn/utils/benchmark.py:1-269]()

The `benchmark_backward` function clears `.grad` on all tensor inputs before each timed iteration and calls `y.backward(grad, retain_graph=True)`. The `grad` tensor is allocated once from `torch.randn_like(y)` before the timed loop begins.

[flash_attn/utils/benchmark.py:30-69]()

### `flash_attn/cute/benchmark.py`

The newer Python CuTe DSL benchmark script (`benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py`) imports from `flash_attn.cute.benchmark` rather than `flash_attn.utils.benchmark`. The exported names (`benchmark_forward`, `benchmark_backward`, `benchmark_combined`, `benchmark_all`, `benchmark_fwd_bwd`, `pytorch_profiler`) mirror the older module's API.

[benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:24]()

## `time_fwd` — Lightweight Per-call Timer

Both `hopper/benchmark_attn.py` and `benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py` define a local `time_fwd` helper that delegates to `triton.testing.do_bench`:

```python
# hopper/benchmark_attn.py:41-59
def time_fwd(func, *args, repeats=30, verbose=True, desc="", **kwargs):
    return Timing(do_bench(lambda: func(*args, **kwargs), warmup=3, rep=repeats) * 1e-3)
```

The return value is a `Timing` named tuple with a single `.mean` field expressed in **seconds**. This is distinct from `benchmark_forward`, which returns a `torch.utils.benchmark.Measurement` object.

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:18-59](), [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:18-66]()

---

## FLOP Calculation

Two variants of a `flops` function exist in the codebase.

### Simple variant (`benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py`)

[benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py:27-30]()

```
flops(batch, seqlen, headdim, nheads, causal, mode)
```

```
f = 4 × batch × seqlen² × nheads × headdim / (2 if causal else 1)
```

Mode multipliers:

| `mode` | Multiplier |
|---|---|
| `"fwd"` | 1× |
| `"bwd"` | 2.5× |
| `"fwd_bwd"` | 3.5× |

### General variant (`hopper/benchmark_attn.py`, `benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py`)

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:62-73](), [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:69-80]()

```
flops(batch, nheads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k, headdim, headdim_v, causal, window_size)
```

Supports asymmetric sequence lengths, separate head dims for Q/K and V, and sliding-window local attention. The effective KV length per query row is computed as `avg_seqlen`:

- **Full attention**: `avg_seqlen = seqlen_k`
- **Causal**: `avg_seqlen = (max(0, seqlen_k - seqlen_q) + seqlen_k) / 2`
- **Local window**: computed by iterating over query rows and clamping column ranges

Total FLOPs: `batch × nheads × 2 × seqlen_q × avg_seqlen × (headdim + headdim_v)`

The backward pass uses `2.5 × nFLOPS` when reporting efficiency, applied at the print step rather than inside the function.

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:386-398]()

### `efficiency` helper

[benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py:33-34]()

```python
def efficiency(flop, time):
    return (flop / time / 10**12) if not math.isnan(time) else 0.0
```

Returns TFLOPs/s. The newer scripts compute this inline at the print step: `nFLOPS / m.mean * 1e-12`.

---

## Result Storage Convention

All benchmark scripts accumulate results into two plain dicts: `time_f` and `time_b`.

```
key:   (causal, headdim, batch_size, seqlen), method_name
value: elapsed time in seconds (float)
```

Example key: `(True, 128, 2, 8192), "Flash3"`. Results can optionally be serialized with `pickle` for later analysis.

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:245-246](), [benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py:85-87]()

---

## Configuration Parameters

The benchmark scripts are configured via module-level variables, not command-line arguments.

| Variable | Description | Typical values |
|---|---|---|
| `repeats` | Iteration count for each timed call | 10–30 |
| `bs_seqlen_vals` | List of `(batch_size, seqlen)` pairs to sweep | `[(2, 8192)]` |
| `headdim` | Head dimension for Q/K | 64, 128, 256 |
| `nheads_kv` | Number of KV heads (set to `nheads` for MHA, `nheads // N` for GQA) | varies |
| `causal` | Whether to benchmark causal masking | `[False, True]` |
| `varlen` | Enable variable-length sequence mode | `False` |
| `dtype` | Data type | `torch.bfloat16`, `torch.float8_e4m3fn` |
| `page_size` | Paged KV cache page size (`None` to disable) | `None`, `128` |
| `softcap` | Tanh softcap value | `0.0`, `15.0` |
| `deterministic` | Use deterministic backward | `False` |

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:215-245](), [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:226-255]()

---

## cuDNN SDPA Harness

The `cudnn` package (installed separately as `nvidia-cudnn-frontend`) is used to benchmark cuDNN's SDPA as a baseline. The setup creates a `cudnn.pygraph`, validates it, builds execution plans, and returns a `run()` closure that can be passed directly to `time_fwd`.

**Forward setup**: `cudnn_spda_setup`  
**Backward setup**: `cudnn_spda_bwd_setup`

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:91-212](), [benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py:98-222]()

**Diagram: cuDNN SDPA forward graph construction**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant "caller" as "caller"
    participant "cudnn_spda_setup()" as "cudnn_spda_setup"
    participant "cudnn.pygraph" as "graph"
    participant "run() closure" as "run"

    "caller" ->> "cudnn_spda_setup": "q, k, v, causal, window_size_left"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" ->> "graph": "create pygraph"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" ->> "graph": "graph.tensor_like(q, k, v)"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" ->> "graph": "graph.sdpa(...)"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" ->> "graph": "graph.validate() / build / check_support / build_plans"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" ->> "run": "bind variant_pack + workspace"
    "cudnn_spda_setup" -->> "caller": "return run"
    "caller" ->> "run": "time_fwd(run, repeats=...)"
    "run" ->> "graph": "graph.execute(variant_pack, workspace)"
```

Sources: [hopper/benchmark_attn.py:91-143]()

The cuDNN SDPA benchmarks only run when `headdim <= 256` and `dtype != torch.float8_e4m3fn`. In `benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py`, they also require `headdim == headdim_v`.

---

## Triton Attention Baseline

`hopper/benchmark_attn.py` optionally imports `triton_fused_attention` from `triton_fused_attention` (a separately installed Triton kernel). Tensors must be transposed to `(batch, nheads, seqlen, headdim)` layout before calling it.

```python
qt, kt, vt = [x.detach().transpose(1, 2).contiguous().requires_grad_() for x in [q, k, v]]
m3 = time_fwd(triton_attention, qt, kt, vt, causal, 1 / math.sqrt(headdim), ...)
```

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:336-346]()

In practice, the newer `benchmarks/benchmark_attn.py` sets `triton_attention = None` unconditionally, disabling this baseline.

---

## xFormers Baselines

`benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py` benchmarks two xFormers operator backends:

| Key | Op pair |
|---|---|
| `"xformers.c"` | `xops.fmha.cutlass.FwOp`, `xops.fmha.cutlass.BwOp` |
| `"xformers.f"` | `xops.fmha.flash.FwOp`, `xops.fmha.flash.BwOp` |

Both use `xops.memory_efficient_attention` with `attn_bias=xops.LowerTriangularMask()` for causal mode.

[benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention.py:147-168]()

## Benchmark Flow

**Diagram: Full benchmark loop structure**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["for headdim in headdim_vals"]
    B["for batch_size, seqlen in bs_seqlen_vals"]
    C["Allocate q, k, v tensors\nwith requires_grad=True"]
    D["for causal in False, True"]
    E["nFLOPS = flops(...)"]
    F1["time_fwd(flash_attn_func, ...) -> time_f[key, 'Flash2']"]
    F2["benchmark_backward(flash_attn_func, ...) -> time_b[key, 'Flash2']"]
    G1["time_fwd(cudnn_spda, ...) -> time_f[key, 'cuDNN']"]
    G2["time_fwd(cudnn_spda_bwd, ...) -> time_b[key, 'cuDNN']"]
    H1["time_fwd(flash_attn_func_v3, ...) -> time_f[key, 'Flash3']"]
    H2["benchmark_backward(flash_attn_func_v3, ...) -> time_b[key, 'Flash3']"]
    I["Print: latency ms, TFLOPS"]
    J["time.sleep(1) between each method"]

    A --> B --> C --> D --> E
    E --> F1 --> F2
    F2 --> J --> G1 --> G2 --> J --> H1 --> H2 --> I
    I --> D
```

Sources: [hopper/benchmark_attn.py:270-401]()

The `time.sleep(1)` calls between method benchmarks mitigate power throttling artifacts from back-to-back GPU workloads.

---

## `pytorch_profiler` for Kernel-Level Tracing

[flash_attn/utils/benchmark.py:202-256]()

`pytorch_profiler` runs 30 warm-up iterations, then captures one profiler pass using `torch.profiler.profile`. It prints `prof.key_averages().table(row_limit=50)` and optionally exports a Chrome trace file via `prof.export_chrome_trace(filename)`.

Usage in benchmarks (commented out by default, uncommented as needed):

```python
pytorch_profiler(flash_attn_func_v3, q, k, v, causal=causal, backward=True)
```

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:378-381]()

---

## Reading Benchmark Output

The benchmark scripts print one line per method per configuration:

```
### headdim=128, causal=True, seqlen=8192, batch_size=2, nheads=16, nheads_kv=16 ###
FAv2 fwd:  2.541ms, 312.4 TFLOPS
FAv2 bwd:  6.203ms, 319.8 TFLOPS
CuDNN fwd: 2.617ms, 303.4 TFLOPS
CuDNN bwd: 6.391ms, 310.0 TFLOPS
FAv3 fwd:  2.210ms, 358.9 TFLOPS
FAv3 bwd:  5.612ms, 353.8 TFLOPS
```

The backward TFLOPS line uses `2.5 × nFLOPS / time` because the backward pass performs approximately 2.5× the FLOPs of the forward pass (recomputing attention scores plus computing three gradient tensors).

[hopper/benchmark_attn.py:384-398]()
